items.title: Google DeepMind integrates computer use into Gemini 3.5 Flash to enable cross-platform agent interactions and improve enterprise automation tasks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Google DeepMind has integrated computer use capabilities directly into its Gemini 3.5 Flash model, enhancing its ability to build agents that interact seamlessly across browser, mobile, and desktop platforms. This integration improves performance on complex, long-term tasks such as continuous software testing and enterprise automation, allowing agents to see, reason, and act within various professional applications. Previously available only as a standalone model, computer use is now a native feature of Gemini 3.5 Flash, accessible through the Gemini API and Enterprise Agent Platform. To address security concerns, DeepMind has implemented targeted adversarial training and introduced enterprise safeguards that require user confirmation for sensitive actions and can halt tasks if prompt injection is detected. These measures, combined with recommended best practices like sandboxing and human oversight, aim to ensure safe deployment in live environments.

items.title: OpenAI unveils Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip built by Broadcom, designed to optimize AI model performance and efficiency [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI has introduced Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip developed in partnership with Broadcom to enhance the performance and efficiency of its AI models. The chip is tailored specifically for OpenAI's inference workloads, aiming to deliver better performance-per-watt compared to existing solutions. This move reflects OpenAI's strategy to optimize its AI infrastructure by designing hardware that complements its software and operational needs. Jalapeño focuses on accelerating inference tasks, which involve running pre-trained AI models in response to user inputs, and is expected to reduce operating costs, particularly for real-time applications like coding models. While more demanding processes such as model pre-training may continue to rely on Nvidia GPUs, this chip represents a significant step in OpenAI's efforts to control costs and improve efficiency across its AI stack by integrating custom hardware, software, and data center design.

items.title: Anthropic says Alibaba illicitly extracted capabilities from Claude AI model [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic has accused Alibaba of illicitly extracting capabilities from its Claude AI model. The allegation suggests that Alibaba may have improperly accessed or replicated features of Anthropic's technology, raising concerns about intellectual property and competitive practices in the AI industry. This development highlights ongoing tensions around AI model security and proprietary technology between major companies.

items.title: RubyLLM launches a unified Ruby framework supporting all major AI providers with features for chatbots, AI agents, image generation, transcription, and more [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: RubyLLM has introduced a unified Ruby framework that supports all major AI providers, enabling developers to build chatbots, AI agents, image generation tools, transcription services, and various AI workflows with a consistent interface. The framework simplifies integration by providing a single API for multiple AI models, including GPT, Claude, and local options like Ollama, reducing the complexity of managing different APIs and response formats. The framework offers features such as conversational AI, image and video analysis, audio transcription, document extraction, image generation, embeddings, content moderation, and tool integration for custom Ruby methods. It also supports structured JSON output, real-time streaming responses, Rails integration, asynchronous concurrency, and access to over 800 AI models from providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google VertexAI. RubyLLM aims to streamline AI development in Ruby with minimal dependencies and easy installation.

items.title: Researchers present Sol Video Inference Engine, an agent-native acceleration framework that doubles video diffusion model inference speed with minimal quality loss across diverse models and hardware [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed the Sol Video Inference Engine, a training-free acceleration framework designed to enhance the efficiency of video diffusion models. This framework integrates five optimization techniques-cache, sparse attention, token pruning, quantization, and kernel fusion-into an agent-based system that tailors acceleration strategies to specific combinations of models, hardware, and inference settings. By automating the tuning process with parallel skill agents and human validation, Sol achieves over twice the inference speed while maintaining near-original video quality across diverse video models and hardware platforms. The framework addresses the challenge that acceleration methods often do not generalize well due to variations in model architectures, numerical sensitivities, and hardware capabilities. It was tested on three different video diffusion models of varying sizes and architectures, demonstrating significant speed improvements with minimal quality loss. This approach reduces the need for costly manual performance engineering and offers a scalable solution for efficient video generation in various deployment scenarios.

items.title: Researchers propose MEDIC, a dualistic meta-learning strategy to improve open set domain generalization by balancing inter-domain and inter-class boundaries, outperforming prior methods in experiments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced MEDIC, a novel dualistic meta-learning strategy designed to improve open set domain generalization by balancing decision boundaries across both domain and class distinctions. This approach addresses the challenge of label mismatches between source and target domains, which traditional methods often overlook, by simultaneously optimizing inter-domain and inter-class task splits to better detect unseen classes in new domains. MEDIC overcomes the limitations of previous one-vs-all classifiers that tend to over-reject out-of-distribution data due to imbalanced positive and negative samples. Experimental results demonstrate that MEDIC not only surpasses existing methods in open set scenarios but also maintains strong performance in conventional closed set generalization tasks, highlighting its effectiveness and versatility in domain generalization challenges.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate reinforcement learning for real-time trigger threshold tuning at the Large Hadron Collider, improving signal efficiency and background rate control on real collision data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have applied reinforcement learning to optimize real-time event filtering thresholds at the Large Hadron Collider, enhancing signal detection efficiency while maintaining control over background noise. By treating threshold tuning as a sequential decision-making problem, their approach dynamically adjusts trigger settings based on streaming data, improving performance compared to static, hand-tuned configurations. The team adapted Group-Filtered Policy Optimization (GFPO) for this streaming control task and tested it on two types of triggers: one sensitive to pileup variations and another designed for anomaly detection. Their method increased the time intervals during which background rates stayed within target ranges by up to 56% on real collision data, also boosting signal efficiency without requiring fine-tuning. This work represents the first successful demonstration of reinforcement learning-based trigger control on actual Large Hadron Collider data, with code made publicly available for further research.

items.title: Researchers propose FlowPipe, an LLM-enhanced conditional generative flow network framework for data preparation pipeline construction, improving accuracy by 11.96% and training speed by 12.5x on 74 datasets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed FlowPipe, a novel framework that enhances the construction of data preparation pipelines for machine learning by integrating large language model (LLM) capabilities with conditional generative flow networks. This approach addresses challenges in automating pipeline synthesis, such as complex operator sequences and inefficient exploration, by modeling the process as conditional probabilistic flow generation over a directed acyclic graph. FlowPipe incorporates deep semantic modulation using LLM-derived logical priors and failure awareness to improve policy decisions and avoid invalid states. Tests on 74 real-world datasets across two benchmark suites demonstrate that FlowPipe outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 11.96% and training convergence that is 12.5 times faster. The framework's source code has been made publicly available, supporting further research and application in automated data preparation for machine learning.

items.title: Researchers find a consistent geometric gap between detection and control directions in language models, showing detection does not imply steerability across multiple models and scales [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified a consistent geometric gap between the directions in language models that detect behaviors and those that control them, challenging the assumption that detection implies steerability. By measuring the angle between the detection and control directions across multiple models and scales, they found a significant misalignment, with cosine similarities far from the ideal value of 1 that would indicate direct control. This gap persists across different models and remains unchanged before and after instruction tuning, suggesting it originates during pretraining. The study shows that while models can perfectly detect certain behaviors, such as hallucinations, the direction that triggers a refusal to produce such outputs is distinct and only partially aligned. Attempts to bridge this gap through rotation improve control but do not fully resolve it. Importantly, the researchers found that the geometric measure of alignment does not predict steerability, indicating that control depends on functional factors beyond static geometric relationships. This work highlights a fundamental dissociation between knowing a behavior and steering it within language models.

items.title: Researchers introduce a 32,534-response double-marked GCSE dataset and find large language models agree with examiners as closely as examiners agree with each other across five subjects [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced a dataset comprising 32,534 double-marked student responses from UK GCSE mock exams across five subjects, including handwritten work. They evaluated whether large language models (LLMs) agree with human examiners as closely as examiners agree with each other. The study found that top-performing LLMs often matched or exceeded the agreement levels between examiners, performing well on subjective tasks like English essays and complex handwritten math scripts. The dataset spans 328 questions and reflects real exam conditions, providing a robust benchmark for automated grading. The models' agreement with examiners was consistent across subjects and did not heavily depend on model size, suggesting that cost-effective automated marking solutions are feasible. This research highlights the potential for LLMs to assist or augment human examiners in educational assessment.

items.title: Researchers analyze entropy dynamics in intermediate layers of large language models to detect jailbreak attacks without additional training across multiple architectures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified that jailbreak attacks on aligned large language models (LLMs), which prompt policy-violating responses despite safety measures, can be detected by analyzing entropy dynamics within the models' intermediate layers. By examining token-level predictive entropy trajectories across layers using the logit lens, they found that changes in entropy over token positions provide a stronger signal of harmful intent than static entropy statistics. This signal is most pronounced in the mid-network layers rather than the final output layer. The study tested multiple LLM architectures, including Llama, Qwen, and Gemma, and demonstrated that these entropy dynamics consistently distinguish jailbreak behavior without requiring additional training. These findings clarify how harmful intent is encoded internally and suggest that monitoring intermediate uncertainty patterns could improve defenses against jailbreak attacks in large language models.

items.title: Researchers present iLLaDA, an 8B masked diffusion language model with bidirectional attention, showing improved performance on general, math, and code benchmarks after training on 12T tokens and fine-tuning on 25B tokens [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced iLLaDA, an 8-billion-parameter masked diffusion language model that employs fully bidirectional attention and is trained from scratch. The model was pre-trained on 12 trillion tokens and fine-tuned on a 25 billion-token instruction dataset, maintaining the masked diffusion objective throughout. iLLaDA demonstrates significant improvements over previous models like LLaDA across general, mathematical, and coding benchmarks, showing competitive performance despite its non-autoregressive training approach. iLLaDA incorporates variable-length generation for efficiency and uses confidence-based scoring for multiple-choice evaluations. Notably, iLLaDA-Base improved by 21.6 points on the BBH benchmark and 14.9 points on ARC-Challenge, while iLLaDA-Instruct showed gains of 14.5 points on MATH and 16.5 points on HumanEval. These results suggest that fully bidirectional diffusion training is a promising method for developing strong language models. The model weights and code are publicly available for further research and development.

items.title: Researchers find that language models with lossy memory producing stale conclusions perform worse than models with empty memory, introducing reclaim evaluation to measure correctability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that language models with lossy memory-where incorrect conclusions are retained but the supporting reasoning is lost-perform worse than models with no memory at all. This phenomenon, termed brittle memory, causes models to confidently produce stale or incorrect answers, whereas models with empty memory tend to abstain. The study introduces reclaim evaluation, a method that compresses interactions and tests whether corrections can recover the correct answers, highlighting that the ability to correct errors depends on preserving the original source information rather than the model's capability. The researchers demonstrate that a source-first policy, which prioritizes keeping the recomputable source over derived conclusions, can restore correctability within the same memory budget when the source is compact and identifiable. This approach was validated across multiple models and real dialogue datasets, showing that errors in dropped sources can propagate and become uncorrectable over time, while the source-first method limits this effect. The study provides a controlled analysis with exact scoring and matched controls, and the authors have released the evaluation tools and conditions for further research.

items.title: Researchers introduce BiPACE, a bisimulation-guided policy optimization method with action counterfactual estimation for LLM agents, improving validation success rates on ALFWorld and Qwen benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed BiPACE, a new bisimulation-guided policy optimization method that enhances the training of long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents by addressing limitations in existing stepwise group-based reinforcement learning approaches. BiPACE improves credit assignment by clustering steps based on behavioral similarity and applying action-conditioned peer baselines, eliminating the need for a learned critic or additional rollouts. This method significantly boosts validation success rates on benchmarks such as ALFWorld and Qwen, outperforming previous techniques like GiGPO and GRPO across multiple model scales. BiPACE works by reducing the mismatch between state and action credit assignment through a novel clustering technique that uses the actor's hidden-state geometry as a proxy for bisimulation. Its Q-style estimator nonparametrically calculates local advantages, leading to more accurate policy updates. Experimental results show that BiPACE achieves higher success rates with only a modest increase in training time, demonstrating its efficiency and effectiveness in optimizing LLM agent policies. The introduction of BiPACE marks a meaningful advancement in reinforcement learning for LLM agents, offering a practical and scalable solution to improve policy optimization without added complexity. The researchers have made the code publicly available, facilitating further exploration and adoption of this approach in the development of more capable and reliable AI agents.

items.title: Researchers introduce Weave of Formal Thought, a method combining rigorous syntactic validation and learned structural representations to improve code generation in large language models, reducing Python token cross-entropy by 14.3% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Weave of Formal Thought (WoFT), a new approach that combines strict syntactic validation with learned structural representations to enhance code generation in large language models. This method introduces a formal engine and constrained decoder based on the full Tree-sitter specification, ensuring that generated code tokens always form valid program prefixes. Additionally, WoFT employs a latent-variable fine-tuning technique that integrates non-terminal grammar symbols into the generation process, allowing the model to retain important structural information adaptively. By fine-tuning the StarCoder2-3B model on Python code using this approach, the researchers achieved a 14.3% reduction in per-token cross-entropy compared to a text-only baseline. This improvement demonstrates that incorporating discretionary latent syntax helps recover critical structural details that traditional flat autoregressive training methods tend to overlook, potentially leading to more accurate and syntactically valid code generation.

items.title: arXiv: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI offers a comprehensive reference on building autonomous AI systems from foundational LLM architecture to multi-agent coordination and production deployment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: "The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI" is a detailed practitioner's reference that explores the development of autonomous AI systems from foundational large language model (LLM) architecture to full production deployment. The guide emphasizes the importance of understanding every layer of the AI pipeline, covering topics such as transformer architecture, training techniques, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and advanced reasoning models. It also addresses agentic AI concepts including memory systems, agent design patterns, inter-agent communication protocols, and multi-agent architectures. The book combines theoretical foundations with practical implementation advice, featuring code examples and references to primary literature. It concludes with discussions on agent development frameworks, user interface design for agentic systems, evaluation methodologies, and strategies for deploying these systems in production environments.

items.title: Researchers analyze why accumulated orthogonal transformations improve length extrapolation in attention models but degrade at extreme context lengths, with experiments supporting theoretical predictions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have investigated why accumulated orthogonal transformations, such as those used in PaTH Attention, improve length extrapolation in attention models but experience performance degradation at extreme context lengths. By studying a variant that replaces position-indexed angles with accumulated token-dependent rotations, they found a similar pattern of initial improvement followed by decline. Their theoretical analysis shows that accumulated orthogonal transformations become incoherent after many steps, suppressing attention to distant tokens and creating a finite mixing window independent of context length, which explains the observed behavior. The study further demonstrates that while accumulated rotations enhance extrapolation beyond training lengths, they inevitably degrade without explicit control of far-token contributions. Experiments confirm these findings, showing that random and learned token-dependent rotations improve extrapolation compared to traditional methods, and that rotating values alongside queries and keys extends the effective range. However, models relying solely on rotations still degrade at very long contexts, whereas methods like ALiBi maintain stable performance, highlighting the importance of managing far-token influence in attention mechanisms.

items.title: Researchers introduce Taxonomic Strategy Retrieval to reduce compounding errors in foundation-model agents during multi-step persuasion tasks, improving win rates and argumentative efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Taxonomic Strategy Retrieval (TS-RAG) to address compounding errors in foundation-model agents during multi-step persuasion tasks. These agents often face challenges where early mistakes affect long-term outcomes, especially in subjective environments like persuasion. TS-RAG introduces a categorical bottleneck that separates argumentative structure from content, reducing semantic leakage seen in standard retrieval methods and improving logical consistency. Evaluations show that TS-RAG enhances the transfer of abstract logic across domains and enables less complex persuader agents to outperform stronger opponents, increasing win rates from 70.5% to 78.5% while boosting argumentative efficiency. The study also presents a Debate State Representation for detailed diagnostics, highlighting the importance of strict constraints to prevent evaluation failures caused by agent conformity.

items.title: Researchers find thinking tokens in reasoning models rarely change safety outcomes and often lead to over-refusal, challenging assumptions about deliberative safety behavior [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have examined the role of "thinking tokens" in advanced reasoning models, which are believed to enhance performance and safety by allowing models to deliberate before responding. Their study across several leading open-weight models found that the final decision to comply or refuse a request is largely determined early in the process, with little change during the subsequent thinking phase. This suggests that the apparent deliberation is more a form of prefix completion than genuine reconsideration. The study also revealed that current safety interventions, designed to encourage deliberation, tend to increase over-refusal and suppress the limited deliberation signals present. These findings challenge the assumption that thinking tokens inherently improve safety and highlight the need for new methods that foster authentic safety deliberation in reasoning models.

items.title: Researchers introduce LLM-ACES, a closed-loop framework using large language models for adaptive discovery of dynamical system equations, outperforming baselines on 122 ODE benchmarks with higher accuracy and sample efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed LLM-ACES, a closed-loop framework that uses large language models to adaptively discover governing equations of dynamical systems from data. Unlike traditional methods that rely on fixed datasets, LLM-ACES iteratively refines symbolic hypotheses and guides data acquisition based on disagreements among candidate equations, improving accuracy and efficiency in identifying ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Tested on 122 ODE systems from ODEBench and ODEBase, LLM-ACES outperformed state-of-the-art baselines by achieving significantly lower median normalized mean square error and higher symbolic accuracy. The framework demonstrated robustness to noise and required only a fraction of the data compared to existing approaches, effectively recovering correct symbolic structures without introducing spurious terms. This adaptive, feedback-driven approach addresses challenges in modeling complex dynamical systems with limited data, offering a more reliable and sample-efficient method for discovering underlying equations. Its success suggests potential for broader applications in scientific domains where accurate modeling of dynamical behavior is critical.

items.title: Researchers present ASAP, an agent-system co-design using LLMs to integrate diverse hyperparameter optimizers and reduce wall-clock time in machine learning experiments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced ASAP, a novel agent-system co-design that enhances hyperparameter optimization (HPO) in machine learning by integrating multiple hyperparameter optimizers using large language models (LLMs). ASAP addresses limitations of previous methods that relied on single-tool LLM replacements and iteration-based evaluations, which failed to handle diverse problems and did not reduce actual wall-clock time. By combining diverse optimizers and redesigning the optimization loop, ASAP improves efficiency and reduces total runtime without sacrificing performance. ASAP leverages the reasoning capabilities of LLMs to select proposals from a pool of inductive-biased optimizers each round. Its system design includes a prefix-stable prompt to maximize cache reuse, speculation parallelism to hide latency during model evaluation, and a Self-Tuner that adapts execution parameters dynamically. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ASAP consistently outperforms existing baselines across various modern HPO tasks, highlighting the benefits of integrating multiple tools and co-designing agent and system components for practical machine learning optimization.

items.title: Researchers present Argus benchmark evaluating 35 uncertainty quantification methods across 4 vision-language models and GUI grounding datasets, revealing stability limits and calibration challenges [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Argus, a comprehensive benchmark evaluating 35 post-hoc uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods across four vision-language models (VLMs) and multiple GUI grounding datasets. This benchmark assesses the stability and calibration of UQ methods critical for computer-use agents that convert VLM predictions into executable GUI actions, highlighting challenges in maintaining reliable uncertainty estimates across different models and interfaces. The study reveals that while UQ rankings remain stable across datasets for a fixed model, they degrade significantly when applied across different model classes or observable interfaces, emphasizing the need for model-specific calibration. Argus includes a 27-method open-weight matrix and an 8-method closed-source matrix, covering a range of techniques such as logit-based scores, sampling measures, hidden-state and density estimators, attention-based scores, and verbalized confidence prompting. The findings show that hidden-state and density-based methods offer the most stable performance among open-weight approaches, whereas certain methods like CoCoA-1MCA and verbalized self-assessment excel in specific scenarios. The benchmark also demonstrates that uncertainty rankings transfer well within models but poorly to closed-source vendors, suggesting that UQ methods should be recalibrated for each target system. The research further indicates that score-level discrimination alone is insufficient for deployment, as conformal click regions shrink significantly when UQ is calibrated but suffer coverage loss under calibration-test or interface mismatches. To support further development, the authors have released detailed records, calibration and test splits, UQ scores, and analysis tools to facilitate regime-aware selection of uncertainty quantification methods in GUI agents.

items.title: Researchers present a space-efficient streaming algorithm for language generation with polynomial memory bounds and characterize memory requirements for exact identification in DFA-recognized languages
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a space-efficient streaming algorithm for language generation that operates within polynomial memory bounds. The algorithm focuses on languages recognized by deterministic finite automata (DFAs) with limited states and alphabet size, aiming to produce a hypothesis language that closely approximates the target language while minimizing omitted strings. They demonstrate that exact identification of the target language requires exponential space, but their polynomial-space algorithm achieves a bounded generation gap and captures all sufficiently long strings in the target language. The study establishes a clear boundary between polynomial-space approximate generation and exponential-space exact identification by providing both an upper bound algorithm and a near-matching lower bound derived from communication complexity. This work advances the understanding of memory requirements for language learning in streaming settings and highlights the trade-offs between memory usage and accuracy in language generation tasks.

items.title: Researchers introduce Autodata, an AI agent trained to act as a data scientist creating high quality synthetic training and evaluation data with improved performance across multiple reasoning tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Autodata, an AI agent designed to function as a data scientist by generating high-quality synthetic training and evaluation data. This method involves training the agent through meta-optimization to enhance its ability to produce stronger datasets, leading to improved performance across various reasoning tasks including computer science research, legal reasoning, and mathematical problem-solving. The team implemented a practical approach called Agentic Self-Instruct and demonstrated that meta-optimizing the data scientist agent itself results in even greater performance gains compared to traditional synthetic data creation methods. This agentic data creation approach offers a novel way to leverage increased computational resources for producing higher quality training data, potentially transforming the process of building AI datasets.

items.title: Researchers find small language models can unlearn previously acquired rules during pretraining based on corpus support frequency, with asymmetric control over rule survival and no recovery after removal [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have discovered that small language models can unlearn previously acquired linguistic rules during pretraining, a phenomenon they term "natural ungrokking." In experiments, a model initially learned to correctly associate pronouns with gendered names but later lost this ability despite continued exposure to supporting data. The survival of learned rules depends on how frequently the training corpus reinforces them, with competing patterns able to displace established rules without leaving traces in the loss curve. The study found that the frequency of rule support in the training data predicts whether a rule persists, while the ratio of data to model parameters influences the extent of rule degradation. This dynamic was observed across multiple training runs and model scales, including public Pythia checkpoints. Notably, once a rule is lost, attempts to restore it by reintroducing strong supporting evidence fail, indicating an asymmetric control over rule retention. These findings highlight the complex interplay between training data and model behavior during pretraining and suggest limitations in the reversibility of learned knowledge.

items.title: Researchers analyze climate discourse differences between paid Meta ads and organic Bluesky posts from July 2024 to September 2025 using interpretable thematic discovery with large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers conducted a comparative analysis of climate discourse between paid advertisements on Meta and organic posts on Bluesky from July 2024 to September 2025. They developed an interpretable thematic discovery method using large language models to cluster and label text themes without predefined topics. The study found that paid ads focus on promoting specific climate solutions in a formal and forward-looking manner, while organic posts emphasize systemic critique with a crisis-oriented, scientific perspective. The analysis highlights systematic differences in how climate change is discussed across these platforms, reflecting the distinct nature of institutionally produced messaging versus user-driven conversation. The researchers also demonstrated the practical value of their thematic approach through tasks like stance prediction and theme-guided retrieval. Although centered on climate communication, the framework can be applied to analyze thematic differences across various communication environments.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate zero-shot cross-lingual confidence estimation in multilingual large language models using a monolingually trained linear probe without target-language retraining [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a method for zero-shot cross-lingual confidence estimation in multilingual large language models (LLMs) using a linear probe trained only on a single language. This probe predicts the correctness of answers in open-ended question answering tasks by analyzing intermediate model representations and generalizes effectively to diverse, unseen languages without requiring retraining on target languages. The study reveals that confidence-related features are concentrated in the middle layers of LLMs across different languages, indicating a shared confidence subspace. The approach offers a strong baseline for confidence estimation that compares favorably with existing methods, especially since its zero-shot performance depends on the similarity between the source and target languages. This work addresses the common limitation of prior confidence estimation techniques that often degrade or need retraining when applied to multiple languages, highlighting the potential for more robust multilingual applications of LLMs.

items.title: Researchers propose Streaming-dLLM, a training-free framework that accelerates diffusion large language models up to 68.2X by pruning suffix tokens and using dynamic decoding with early exit [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Streaming-dLLM, a training-free framework designed to accelerate diffusion large language models (dLLMs) by up to 68.2 times. This approach addresses inefficiencies in the block-wise diffusion process by pruning redundant suffix tokens and employing a dynamic decoding strategy with an early exit mechanism, which skips unnecessary iterations for tokens that have already converged. Streaming-dLLM maintains generation quality while significantly speeding up inference. The framework improves spatial efficiency through attenuation-guided suffix modeling, which approximates full context by removing less informative tokens. Temporally, it adapts the denoising schedule dynamically based on confidence levels, enhancing decoding speed without retraining the model. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of Streaming-dLLM in optimizing diffusion decoding processes.

items.title: Researchers propose Memini, an associative memory model with multi-timescale dynamics for continual knowledge updating in large language models, inspired by biological synaptic consolidation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have proposed Memini, an associative memory model designed to enable continual knowledge updating in large language models (LLMs). Inspired by biological synaptic consolidation, Memini organizes knowledge as a directed graph with edges that carry two coupled internal variables operating on different timescales. This design aims to replicate biological memory dynamics, allowing new associations to be immediately usable, reinforcing repeated information, and enabling selective forgetting through a unified mechanism. Memini applies the Benna-Fusi model of synaptic consolidation to external memory, reframing it as a learning substrate that adapts through its own internal dynamics rather than explicit management. This approach is intended to address the challenge that LLMs, typically trained once, face when deployed in constantly changing environments. The article presents an early-stage conceptual design and does not include experimental evaluation.

items.title: daVinci-kernel introduces a reinforcement learning framework with co-evolving skill selection, summarization, and utilization for GPU kernel optimization, outperforming prior RL models on KernelBench [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: daVinci-kernel is a reinforcement learning framework designed to optimize GPU kernel performance by dynamically evolving a library of reusable skills. It integrates three agents-a Skill Selection Agent that identifies relevant techniques, a Policy Agent that generates CUDA/Triton kernels based on selected skills, and a Skill Summary Agent that distills successful strategies-sharing a single large language model backbone. This approach ensures that only skills verified to improve execution speed are added, and the system is trained end-to-end using multi-turn reinforcement learning methods. daVinci-kernel was evaluated on KernelBench, where its 14-billion parameter model achieved superior performance across multiple levels compared to previous reinforcement learning models, notably outperforming the prior leading model, Dr. Kernel-14B. The framework's combination of skill discovery, selection, and summarization represents a significant advancement in automated GPU kernel optimization.

items.title: Researchers identify Memory Contagion, showing evaluator bias propagates across time in LLM agent memories even with perfect consolidation, with bias type and model generation affecting susceptibility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called Memory Contagion, where evaluator bias propagates across time through the memory systems of Large Language Model (LLM) agents. Their study shows that when agents are influenced by biased evaluators, these biases become embedded in their experiences and persist in memory, affecting future agents even with perfect memory consolidation. The research highlights that susceptibility to this bias depends on the type of bias and the generation of the model, with length preference bias spreading in older models but not in newer ones, while authority bias does not propagate through memory in the tested scenarios. The study involved experiments across different bias types and model versions, revealing that length bias can propagate at contamination rates as low as 20%, and that consolidation processes can either reduce or amplify bias depending on its nature. These findings expose a significant vulnerability in current agent memory designs and provide formal methods to measure how bias can persist and spread over time within LLM agent memories.

items.title: Researchers propose NaviGen to convert user interaction history into executable instructions for personalized multimodal content generation, improving image and video synthesis across multiple domains [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced NaviGen, a novel approach that converts a user's interaction history into executable instructions to enhance personalized multimodal content generation, including images and videos. This method addresses challenges in encoding user behavior into a form understandable by language models and developing instruction-writing capabilities absent in existing data. NaviGen uses a dual identifier system combining collaborative and textual codes, enabling a two-stage training process that refines preference reasoning and aligns content generation with user intent through hierarchical rewards. Tests across various domains such as products, games, and short videos demonstrate that NaviGen improves the specificity, relevance, and visual quality of generated content while also enhancing next-item prediction. The approach bridges the gap between user behavior and content synthesis, offering a more tailored and effective generation experience. The researchers have made their code publicly available to support further development in this area.

items.title: Researchers introduce DigenRL, a disaggregated reinforcement learning framework for diffusion-based generative large language models, achieving 1.56-2.10x throughput improvements over existing systems on 16-32 GPU testbeds [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed DigenRL, a disaggregated reinforcement learning framework designed for diffusion-based generative large language models (LLMs). This new system improves throughput by 1.56 to 2.10 times compared to existing diffusion RL systems like veRL-Omni and GenRL, by enabling flexible resource allocation, heterogeneous GPU support, and efficient task scheduling across 16 to 32 GPU testbeds. DigenRL introduces innovations such as a generation-axis pipeline and time-step parallelism to enhance pipelining between rollout and training phases, an elastic trainer-assisted generation method that allows trainer GPUs to assist with rollout tasks dynamically, and a tightly constrained asynchronous strategy to optimize pipeline utilization. These advancements address limitations in current colocated execution models, which restrict resource scaling and deployment flexibility. Extensive experiments using various generative models, including HunyuanVideo-13B and QwenImage-20B, demonstrate DigenRL's effectiveness in accelerating diffusion-based RL training. This framework represents a significant step toward more efficient and scalable reinforcement learning systems for visual generative LLMs.

items.title: BluTrain releases C++/CUDA AI training framework with native layers, outperforming PyTorch in throughput and memory efficiency on 124M-parameter GPT-2 model [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: BluTrain is a new AI training framework developed in C++ and CUDA that offers precise control over hardware execution while simplifying system complexity. Designed from the ground up, it features native implementations of all layers, including a typed tensor module with reverse-mode autograd, a linear algebra library, and a multi-mode distributed execution module. In tests training a 124M-parameter GPT-2 model on an 8-GPU system, BluTrain demonstrated superior performance compared to PyTorch, achieving higher throughput and up to 22% better memory efficiency without compromising numerical accuracy or model convergence. The framework's architecture allows for extensive native tuning at every layer, enabling further performance improvements. By focusing on system-level optimization rather than just model architecture, BluTrain aims to set a new standard for efficient and scalable deep learning training.

items.title: Workshop report outlines challenges and solutions for engineering reliable autonomous systems, focusing on verification, real-world deployment, and safe software architectures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent workshop report from the Lorentz Center Workshop "Engineering Reliable Autonomous Systems" (ERAS) highlights key challenges and solutions in developing dependable autonomous systems. The event, held in June 2024 and co-organized by the FMAS and AREA communities, brought together researchers, industry experts, and sector representatives to focus on verification and validation techniques, real-world system engineering, and safe software architectures. The report presents a comprehensive catalogue of challenges and proposes pathways to address them, emphasizing both existing academic methods not yet widely adopted in practice and areas requiring further research. The workshop aimed to bridge gaps between academic research and industrial application by fostering collaboration and outlining a roadmap for future efforts. This initiative is intended to support ongoing advancements in autonomous system reliability, ensuring safer and more effective deployment across various sectors where these technologies are increasingly prevalent.

items.title: Researchers present AutoSpec, a framework using inductive logic programming to evolve interpretable safety rules for LLM agents, achieving up to 94% false positive reduction and high recall across code execution and embodied agent domains [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed AutoSpec, a framework that uses inductive logic programming to automatically refine safety rules for large language model (LLM) agents. By evolving expert-designed rules based on user annotations of safe and unsafe behaviors, AutoSpec significantly reduces false positives while maintaining high recall, achieving up to a 94% reduction in false positives and improving rule accuracy across code execution and embodied agent tasks. The approach iteratively identifies key predicates to adjust rules, producing interpretable and auditable safety guidelines that generalize well to new scenarios. AutoSpec operates by analyzing execution traces to find false-positive and false-negative examples, then uses inductive logic programming to generate and verify candidate rule modifications. This process converges within a few iterations, outperforming heuristic methods by up to 4.8 times in F1 score. The resulting rules balance precision and recall effectively, addressing the limitations of brittle hand-crafted rules and opaque neural classifiers in safety-critical applications.

items.title: Researchers propose DynamicPO, a framework to prevent preference optimization collapse in LLM-based recommendation systems by prioritizing boundary-critical negatives and adjusting optimization strength dynamically [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called preference optimization collapse in large language model-based recommendation systems, where increasing negative samples paradoxically degrades performance despite lower training loss. This occurs because easily distinguishable negatives overshadow boundary-critical negatives that define user preferences, weakening the model's decision boundary. To address this, they propose DynamicPO, a framework that dynamically selects informative negatives near decision boundaries and adjusts optimization strength based on boundary ambiguity. DynamicPO integrates two adaptive mechanisms: Dynamic Boundary Negative Selection and Dual-Margin Dynamic beta Adjustment. Experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that DynamicPO effectively prevents optimization collapse and enhances recommendation accuracy with minimal computational cost. The framework is designed to be lightweight and easily integrated into existing multi-negative preference optimization methods, with code and datasets publicly available.

items.title: Researchers find that a small group of Wikipedia editors significantly influences large language models' handling of animal welfare topics through targeted content edits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated that a small group of Wikipedia editors, known as the Pro-Animal Wikipedians (PAW), can significantly influence how large language models (LLMs) address animal welfare topics by making targeted edits to Wikipedia articles. Their 125 edits across 115 pages were found to heavily impact LLM responses, with models attributing a majority of relevant content to these edits specifically for animal welfare queries. Using advanced data attribution techniques on models like Llama 3.1 and Llama 3.2, the study showed that PAW edits consistently ranked as the most influential sources for animal welfare-related questions, while having little effect on unrelated queries. Fine-tuning models on PAW content further improved their performance on animal welfare texts, confirming that coordinated Wikipedia editing campaigns can measurably shape the values and outputs of language models on specific topics.

items.title: Researchers propose error-aware TF-IDF retrieval-augmented generation framework for ASR error correction, improving hit rate from 53.7% to 90.9% and reducing word error rate from 23.06% to 18.83% on Persian FLEURS dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed an error-aware TF-IDF retrieval-augmented generation framework to improve automatic speech recognition (ASR) error correction, particularly for low-resource languages. This new approach addresses common issues such as hallucination of rare entities and domain-specific terms by integrating a symmetric text normalization module with an error-aware TF-IDF algorithm that prioritizes corrective documents based on historical errors. Tested on the Persian subset of the FLEURS dataset, the method increased the error-aware hit rate from 53.7% to 90.9% and reduced the word error rate from 23.06% to 18.83%, achieving these improvements with minimal inference latency.

items.title: Researchers propose Dustin, a sparse verification framework that speeds up long-context speculative decoding by over 9x with minimal accuracy loss on Qwen2.5-72B at 32k sequence length [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Dustin, a sparse verification framework that significantly accelerates long-context speculative decoding in large language models. By combining lookahead signals from a draft model with historical attention from the target model, Dustin efficiently identifies critical tokens for verification, reducing latency caused by Key-Value cache loading. Tested on the Qwen2.5-72B model with a 32k sequence length, Dustin achieved over a 9-fold speedup in end-to-end decoding with minimal loss in accuracy. Dustin addresses limitations of existing compression methods, which either sacrifice accuracy or incur high computational costs during verification. It employs a sparse estimation technique that limits importance scoring to a small subset of attention heads, enabling a 27.85x speedup in self-attention operations. Evaluations on benchmarks like PG-19 and LongBench demonstrate Dustin's effectiveness in improving inference throughput for multi-batch long-context large language models.

items.title: Researchers propose test-time adaptation with semi-supervised learning to improve AI text detection under continual distribution shifts, outperforming commercial models on adversarial examples [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a test-time adaptation method using semi-supervised learning to improve AI text detection amid ongoing distribution shifts, such as adversarial humanization, new large language models, and changes in human writing styles. This approach leverages the homogeneity of unlabeled samples during inference to adapt without requiring labeled data, addressing limitations of current supervised detectors that struggle with these shifts. Their method significantly outperforms commercial models, detecting 90.5% of adversarial AI-generated text compared to 24.1% by a leading commercial detector. The study highlights that existing AI text detectors fail under both adversarial and natural distribution changes, while the proposed test-time adaptation remains robust. The researchers have made their code publicly available, facilitating further development and evaluation of AI text detection techniques that can operate effectively in real-world, dynamic environments.

items.title: Researchers present a taxonomy of conversational memory roles and evaluate their impact on response quality and personalization in large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a detailed taxonomy of conversational memory roles and examined how these different types of memory affect the quality and personalization of responses in large language models (LLMs). Their study highlights that various memory functions, such as clarifying memory, can enhance factual accuracy and personalization, while irrelevant memory can reduce topic relevance and degrade response quality. This work introduces a user-centric evaluation framework that better captures the nuances of conversational responses compared to traditional reference-based methods. Through experiments on long-term datasets and advanced LLMs, the researchers demonstrated that memory roles significantly influence how conversational agents respond under different contexts. Their findings suggest that leveraging specific memory types can improve the personalization and correctness of responses, offering new directions for enhancing conversational AI systems despite the capabilities of current frontier models.

items.title: Researchers develop neural machine translation systems for low-resource Tangkhul-English language pair using ByT5-large and mT5-small models, achieving BLEU score of 39.97 on test set [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed neural machine translation systems for the low-resource Tangkhul-English language pair, using ByT5-large and mT5-small models fine-tuned on a corpus of 38,336 parallel sentences. The primary ByT5-large system achieved a BLEU score of 39.97 on a test set of 3,856 sentences, demonstrating promising results for this under-resourced Tibeto-Burman language spoken in Manipur, India. The study highlights challenges related to Tangkhul's Latin-script diacritics and the domain bias of the training data, which includes biblical texts, stories, and conversational material. The researchers suggest that future improvements could come from diversifying the data and adapting the models to different domains to enhance translation quality further.

items.title: Researchers present a red teaming framework for large language models that uses multi-role models to expose unfaithfulness, increasing adversarial attack success by up to 7.9% in question-answering tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a red teaming framework for large language models (LLMs) that uses a multi-role system involving target, attacker, and jury models to identify vulnerabilities in LLM outputs. This approach effectively generates adversarial prompts that expose unfaithfulness in responses, increasing attack success rates by up to 7.9% in question-answering tasks and revealing reliability weaknesses. The framework adapts across various evaluation tasks, including English question-answering and Arabic summarization, allowing comprehensive comparisons of model vulnerabilities. It highlights how structural constraints and architectural design choices impact model safety more than parameter scaling. While the method excels at cross-model and cross-linguistic vulnerability detection, it faces challenges in fully automating adversarial prompt generation across languages and detecting subtle unfaithfulness that does not involve explicit factual errors. Overall, this multi-role red teaming architecture offers actionable insights into current LLM weaknesses and provides a scalable methodology for ongoing safety evaluation as language models continue to evolve.

items.title: Researchers evaluate calibration and adversarial robustness of automated ASR scoring judges for LLM jailbreaks using 596 human-labeled samples, finding significant reliability and attack resistance differences [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers evaluated the reliability and robustness of automated judges used to score attack-success rates (ASR) in large language model (LLM) jailbreak studies. Using 596 human-labeled samples from the HarmBench dataset, they compared two types of judges-a dedicated safety classifier and general LLM-based judges-against human consensus and subjected them to adversarial attacks. The study found that the classifier tends to over-flag harmful content with high recall, while LLM judges maintain high precision but show inconsistent recall, leading to varying ASR results depending on the judge used. The two judge types also differ significantly in their resistance to adversarial manipulation. LLM judges were highly susceptible to simple framing attacks that altered their decisions 57% to 100% of the time, whereas the dedicated classifier was more resistant to such surface attacks but vulnerable to a white-box gradient-based attack that flipped 70% of confident true positives. An audit confirmed that these attacks did not remove harmful content, indicating that many reported ASR figures relying on automated judges may be unreliable. The researchers recommend that future studies report judge precision and recall based on human-labeled data, adjust ASR metrics accordingly, and include adversarial robustness checks for judges. Their code has been made publicly available to support transparency and further research in this area.

items.title: Researchers use MARBERT model to detect spam and analyze sentiment in 24,513 Arabic tweets to improve Saudi Telecom Company customer service [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a model using MARBERT, a variant of the BERT deep learning framework, to detect spam and analyze sentiment in 24,513 Arabic tweets related to Saudi Telecom Company (STC). The study aims to improve STC's customer service by accurately gauging customer sentiments expressed on Twitter, a preferred platform for STC users to provide feedback. The model was evaluated using precision, recall, and f1-score metrics and showed promising accuracy compared to existing methods. The dataset included tweets categorized as positive, negative, neutral, sarcastic, and indeterminate, reflecting a wide range of customer opinions. This research addresses a gap in natural language processing for Arabic, as most sentiment analysis work has focused on English. By leveraging deep learning techniques tailored for Arabic, the study offers a valuable tool for enhancing customer satisfaction through better understanding of social media feedback.

items.title: Researchers propose Semantic Frame-Level Multi-Task Self-Consistency to improve multi-intent spoken language understanding accuracy in zero-shot MAC-SLU benchmark tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Semantic Frame-Level Multi-Task Self-Consistency (SFL-MTSC), a new framework designed to enhance the accuracy of multi-intent spoken language understanding (SLU) using large language models. This approach addresses inconsistencies in intent-slot structures caused by decoding variability, especially in multi-intent scenarios, by decomposing predictions into intent-specific frames and applying domain-intent grouping and slot-level clustering to assess reliability before forming the final output. Zero-shot testing on the MAC-SLU benchmark demonstrated improvements in slot F1 scores and overall accuracy compared to traditional single-path inference, while maintaining stable intent accuracy across various settings.

items.title: Researchers propose REVERIEMEM, a three-layer memory architecture for book-based role-playing agents that improves knowledge boundary fidelity by 34.6 points and achieves 79% win rate on narrative benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced REVERIEMEM, a novel three-layer memory architecture designed for book-based role-playing agents that enhances the fidelity of knowledge boundaries by 34.6 percentage points and achieves a 79% win rate on narrative benchmarks. This system addresses common issues in long-narrative role-playing, such as characters using facts beyond their perspective and maintaining a monotonous style, by structuring memory into episodic, semantic, and personality layers that capture scene memories, visibility-tagged facts, and situation-dependent behaviors respectively. To evaluate REVERIEMEM, the team developed KBF-QA, a benchmark consisting of 4,386 questions across eight novels to test knowledge boundaries. The architecture's performance on BOOKWORLD's narrative protocol demonstrates significant improvements in both maintaining perspective-bounded memory and generating character-grounded narratives, suggesting its potential to advance the realism and depth of AI-driven role-playing agents.

items.title: Researchers introduce a framework comparing nine RAG scenarios including GraphRAG and Agentic RAG with context optimization, showing 19%-53% token usage reduction and identifying retrieval-generation gaps [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a comprehensive framework to evaluate and compare nine different Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) scenarios, including advanced variants like GraphRAG and Agentic RAG. Their study addresses practical use cases involving semi-structured knowledge bases and introduces a novel context engineering method that reduces token usage by 19% to 53%, improving efficiency in managing text and graph retrievals. The research also highlights a retrieval-generation gap, where increased retrieval does not always lead to proportional improvements in generation quality, suggesting that current retrieval-focused metrics may overestimate the benefits of advanced retrieval techniques. The framework encompasses a range of scenarios from simple document-based retrieval to complex integrations involving hybrid text-graph retrieval, domain knowledge graphs, and multi-step agentic planning. By standardizing these scenarios and conducting extensive experiments, the study offers data-driven insights into when and how to deploy various RAG approaches effectively. This work aims to guide the development of production-ready intelligent RAG systems by clarifying the trade-offs and practical considerations involved in their implementation.

items.title: Researchers compare fine-tuned encoder classifiers and LLM-based judges for safety evaluation of large language model outputs across adversarial datasets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have conducted a systematic comparison between fine-tuned encoder classifiers from the ModernBERT family and large language model (LLM)-based judges to evaluate the safety of LLM outputs in user interactions. Their study assesses whether encoder classifiers can effectively identify harmful content without significant performance loss compared to LLM judges, which are typically slower and more costly to deploy. The evaluation uses various adversarial datasets and benchmarks encoder classifiers against rule-based methods, fine-tuned LLM classifiers, and multiple LLM judge strategies. The study fine-tunes encoder classifiers on judge-labeled data using a majority-voting approach and evaluates them on a gold-standard holdout set, measuring performance with metrics such as F1 score, false negative rate, and precision-recall. Results are analyzed by different attack techniques, including single-turn prompting and context manipulation, to determine where encoder classifiers align with or differ from LLM-based judges. The findings offer insights into when encoder classifiers can serve as efficient, cost-effective alternatives for safety evaluation in large language model applications.

items.title: Researchers propose SARA framework to align routing in sparse Mixture-of-Experts models, improving multilingual performance on low-resource languages across multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced SARA (Semantically Anchored Routing Alignment), a new framework designed to improve the performance of sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models in multilingual settings, particularly for low-resource languages. SARA addresses the challenge where tokens from low-resource languages are routed to different experts than those for high-resource languages, limiting cross-lingual knowledge sharing. By aligning the routing distributions of low-resource languages with those of high-resource languages using a Jensen-Shannon divergence constraint, SARA enhances expert selection consistency across languages. The team tested SARA on two large language models across five low-resource languages and three benchmarks, achieving performance gains over standard instruction tuning methods. For example, improvements of 0.8% and 1.2% were observed on the Qwen3-30B-A3B and Phi-3.5-MoE-instruct models, respectively, on the Global-MMLU benchmark. These results suggest that SARA effectively mitigates performance bottlenecks in low-resource languages and offers a scalable approach to boost multilingual capabilities in sparse MoE architectures.

items.title: Overview of HIPE-2026 evaluation on person-place relation extraction from noisy multilingual historical texts in French, German, and English with 17 teams and 40 runs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: HIPE-2026, the third edition of the HIPE evaluation series, focused on extracting temporally grounded person-place relations from noisy, multilingual historical texts in French, German, and English. The challenge involved determining whether a person was present at a location and when, using datasets from nineteenth and twentieth-century newspapers and early modern French literary texts. Seventeen teams participated, submitting over 40 runs that employed various methods ranging from large language models to lightweight classifiers. The evaluation featured a three-fold framework assessing predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, and cross-domain generalization to address the practical needs of processing large-scale historical documents in cultural heritage contexts. Results highlighted the trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness in historical relation extraction, providing insights into current capabilities and challenges in this area. The paper presents detailed system descriptions, datasets, and findings, offering a comprehensive overview of temporally grounded relation extraction for historical documents.

items.title: Researchers introduce SpeechEQ, a benchmark and dataset for evaluating emotional intelligence in speech-language models across 2,265 dialogues and 15 EQ subscales [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed SpeechEQ, a new benchmark and dataset designed to evaluate the emotional intelligence of speech-language models in multi-turn dialogues. The framework includes 2,265 dialogues annotated across 15 emotional quotient subscales based on EQ-i 2.0 theory, along with a Spoken EQ (SEQ) score to assess sociolinguistic reasoning in conversational AI. This approach addresses limitations in current evaluations that focus only on isolated text or passive acoustic cues, overlooking the complex cross-modal reasoning needed for natural human-AI interaction. Experiments using SpeechEQ reveal that existing speech emotion recognition systems and end-to-end speech-language models struggle to fully understand and apply paralinguistic cues. Although end-to-end models perform better than cascaded systems, challenges such as reliance on text shortcuts, alignment safety issues, and contextual memory gaps persist. These findings highlight significant barriers to developing truly emotionally aware AI systems. The SpeechEQ benchmark and a demonstration are publicly available for further research and development.

items.title: Researchers find multi-step tool-use reinforcement learning in large language models can collapse due to control token probability spikes and show supervisory signals improve stability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified that multi-step tool-use reinforcement learning (RL) in large language models (LLMs) can suffer from catastrophic collapse, where performance suddenly deteriorates due to unexpected probability spikes in specific control tokens. This disrupts the structured execution of tasks, although the models' underlying tool-use capabilities remain intact but obscured by formatting issues. The study explores various supervisory signals, such as off-policy supervision and hint-based guidance, applied through different training schemes to address these instabilities. The researchers found that interleaving supervised fine-tuning with RL significantly improves training stability, though it may reduce performance when models face out-of-distribution formats and content. They also examined the effects of learning rates and generalization across different settings. These findings emphasize the importance of combining diverse supervisory signals with RL to enable robust training of LLMs for complex, multi-step tool-use tasks.

items.title: Researchers audit 18 multimodal large language models for order sensitivity, finding 24-50% answer flip rates and limited mitigation from prompt changes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers conducted an audit of 18 leading multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to assess their sensitivity to the order of input data, a key reliability factor often overlooked in standard benchmarks. Using a new method called Facet-Probe, which examines five different facets of input ordering, they found that none of the models were order-invariant, with answer flip rates ranging from 24% to 50%. Even the best-performing model exhibited flips in 13.4% of trials, indicating significant variability in responses depending on input order. The study employed a Bayesian item-response model to distinguish between noise and bias related to ordering and used controls to estimate baseline decoder variability. Attempts to mitigate order sensitivity through prompt modifications showed limited success and were modality-specific, failing to generalize from text to visual reasoning tasks. These findings suggest that prompt-level adjustments alone are insufficient for achieving robust order invariance, highlighting the need for future research into training methods and architectural changes. The authors propose adopting cross-ordering flip rate as a standard metric for evaluating MLLMs.

items.title: Researchers develop reinforcement learning-based adaptive sim-to-real alignment for vibration-based bearing health monitoring under data scarcity, achieving 92.8% accuracy across multiple testbeds [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a reinforcement learning-based method to improve vibration-based bearing health monitoring under conditions of limited operational data. Their approach addresses the challenge of heterogeneous discrepancies between simulated and real-world signals by applying fault-type-specific feature alignment through a continuous-action Markov decision process. This method achieves a high accuracy of 92.8% across multiple testbeds without requiring encoder retraining, demonstrating effective and transferable fault diagnosis capabilities. The technique uses Proximal Policy Optimization to learn adaptive affine corrections that balance minimizing the gap between simulated and real data while preserving the separability of different fault classes. An asymmetry-aware strategy reserves real data for normal conditions and augments fault data with aligned simulations. Validation on datasets from XJTU-SY, CWRU, and a custom slewing bearing testbed confirms the superiority of this reinforcement learning-driven alignment over traditional domain adaptation methods.

items.title: Researchers introduce datasets and methods for learning robust diachronic representations of ancient Greek letterforms across centuries of handwriting variation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed new datasets and methods to improve the learning of robust representations of ancient Greek letterforms, which vary significantly across centuries of handwriting. They introduced three datasets covering different historical periods and proposed techniques including a similarity-weighted supervised contrastive loss and a lacuna-driven augmentation scheme to handle symbolic variation, limited data, and manuscript degradation. Their approach, tested on lightweight CNN and pretrained ResNet models, achieved strong recognition performance and produced embeddings that better distinguish character classes than traditional methods. These embeddings facilitate clustering, identification of stylistic subgroups, and visualization of the diachronic evolution of letterforms, demonstrating the effectiveness of incorporating intrinsic inter-letter relationships and domain-specific augmentations. The researchers provide their code and data publicly, offering a transferable framework for representation learning in contexts with scarce, temporally evolving, and noisy data.

items.title: Researchers argue neural scaling law exponents are fixed by generic mechanisms, urging focus on coefficients to improve large language model performance and compute efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent position paper argues that the exponents in neural scaling laws, which describe how pre-training loss decreases with training time, model size, and compute, are determined by generic mechanisms inherent to model architecture. These include a one-third time scaling from Softmax nonlinearity, inverse width scaling from representational superposition, and inverse depth scaling due to ensemble averaging in Transformer layers. This suggests that current large language models belong to a universality class with fixed exponents. The paper emphasizes that while the exponents remain constant, the coefficients in these scaling laws vary with data and architectural details. These coefficients influence practical aspects such as optimal model design and compute efficiency. The authors propose that focusing research on understanding and optimizing these coefficients could lead to near-term improvements in model performance and potentially reveal new universality classes for future advancements.

items.title: Researchers show emergent capabilities in transformer models arise stochastically from learning sparse attention patterns, with larger models acquiring them earlier on synthetic tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that emergent capabilities in transformer language models, such as pattern completion and indirect object identification, arise stochastically during training rather than smoothly. Larger models tend to acquire these capabilities earlier, which corresponds to the abrupt learning of task-relevant sparse attention patterns. This phenomenon was studied using synthetic datasets, revealing that the difficulty of learning these attention patterns depends on factors like context length and pattern sparsity. The study also showed that increasing the number of attention heads improves learning efficiency, while enlarging the head dimension offers diminishing returns beyond a certain point. Alternative architectures, such as MLP-Mixer, were found to outperform transformers on tasks involving complex attention patterns. These findings provide a mechanistic explanation for the sudden emergence of downstream capabilities in transformer models, linking it to the intrinsic challenge of learning sparse attention patterns.

items.title: Researchers propose MADARA, a model-adaptive routing architecture for cost-efficient multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation, demonstrating up to 50% gains by isolating document context and generalizing across model families [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced MADARA, a model-adaptive routing architecture designed to improve the efficiency of multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) by isolating document context and adapting assessment strategies based on model strength. Their study on 7B-9B instruction-tuned models across various QA benchmarks revealed that for weaker models, isolating documents without complex assessment can yield gains up to 50%, while stronger models benefit from a new label-free probe called Reasoning-Score Coupling to enhance scoring quality. MADARA leverages these insights to provide a lightweight, computationally efficient pipeline that generalizes across different model families without additional training. The research highlights a key distinction in how models benefit from document assessment: weaker baselines gain primarily from resolving multi-document context confusion, whereas stronger baselines require improved scoring mechanisms. MADARA's diagnostic thresholds, derived from a single pilot model, successfully generalize zero-shot to four unseen model families, demonstrating its robustness and potential for broad applicability in cost-efficient RAG systems.

items.title: Researchers propose RAVEN, a visuo-spatio-temporal memory system for long-horizon robotic reasoning and navigation, demonstrating improved efficiency and deployment on Unitree Go1 robot [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed RAVEN, a visuo-spatio-temporal memory system designed to enhance long-horizon robotic reasoning and navigation. RAVEN stores visual embeddings along with spatial and temporal data in a vector database, enabling efficient retrieval grounded in a spatial map to support question answering and goal-directed navigation. This approach bypasses the limitations of image-to-text captioning, allowing for more accurate semantic, spatial, and temporal retrieval at scale. Tested across various simulated and real-world video question-answering benchmarks, RAVEN outperforms caption-based memory systems and matches leading visual language models while reducing retrieval costs by a factor of ten. The system was successfully deployed on a Unitree Go1 robot, demonstrating effective long-horizon navigation and natural language goal-reaching in large indoor environments.

items.title: Sarashina2.2-TTS introduces data scaling and targeted augmentation to improve kanji polyphony disambiguation in Japanese text-to-speech with 361k hours of training data and new pronunciation benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Sarashina2.2-TTS is a new Japanese-focused large language model-based text-to-speech system designed to address the challenge of kanji polyphony, where kanji characters have multiple context-dependent pronunciations. The system is trained on approximately 361,000 hours of speech data, combining Japanese and English, and uses targeted data augmentation covering all 2,136 Joyo kanji to improve pronunciation accuracy. It also introduces the Joyo Kanji Yomi Benchmark and a new evaluation metric, Kana-CER, to measure pronunciation correctness more effectively. Experiments show that Sarashina2.2-TTS achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in kanji-level reading and matches leading systems in sentence-level pronunciation, while also delivering high speaker similarity in zero-shot Japanese speech synthesis. Additionally, it maintains stable Japanese pronunciation across different prompt languages, demonstrating improved cross-lingual robustness due to its balanced training approach.
