items.title: Researchers introduce OscillaTTS with adaptive oscillatory nonlinearity to improve modeling of sharp prosodic dynamics in diffusion-based text-to-speech systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed OscillaTTS, a diffusion-based text-to-speech system that incorporates an adaptive oscillatory nonlinearity to better model sharp prosodic transitions and rapid pitch variations in expressive speech. This approach improves upon existing methods that use fixed periodic nonlinearities, which struggle to capture abrupt changes in amplitude and frequency. OscillaTTS maintains signal stability through a linear bypass component while enabling controllable periodic modulation. Experiments conducted on the LJSpeech and Emotional Speech Dataset demonstrate that OscillaTTS consistently outperforms previous models in both objective and subjective evaluations. These results indicate enhanced capability in modeling expressive prosodic dynamics, suggesting potential advancements in the naturalness and expressiveness of synthesized speech.

items.title: Researchers analyze how harness design affects post-training performance and robustness of tool-integrated LLM agents under task and environment shifts using ALFWorld extension [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have extended the ALFWorld framework to investigate how the design of the harness-the scaffolding that controls tool exposure and information flow-affects the post-training performance and robustness of tool-integrated large language model (LLM) agents. Their study addresses the common assumption of a fixed harness and static environment by treating the harness as a controllable factor and evaluating agent performance under shifts in tasks and tool environments. The findings reveal that harness-aware post-training enhances both in-distribution accuracy and adaptability to out-of-distribution scenarios, while minimal harness design leads to significant performance declines under stronger environment shifts. This work highlights the importance of considering harness design during post-training to improve the resilience of LLM agents when deployed in dynamic settings. By systematically analyzing the interplay between harness configuration and post-training, the study provides insights that could guide the development of more robust and adaptable AI agents capable of handling evolving tasks and environments.

items.title: Researchers introduce the Generalization Spectrum framework to evaluate learning algorithms by measuring transfer distance across test variants in competitive programming tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed the Generalization Spectrum, a new evaluation framework that measures how well learning algorithms generalize from specific training examples to various test scenarios. This framework arranges test variants by increasing transfer distance, from exact recall to more abstract forms of transfer, allowing a detailed analysis of how far knowledge learned from one example can extend. The approach was applied to competitive programming tasks to compare different learning paradigms and their ability to transfer knowledge beyond memorization. The study found that reinforcement learning (RL) converts memorization into near-transfer more effectively than supervised fine-tuning (SFT) baselines, while in-context learning (ICL) shows strong but context-dependent transfer. Further analysis revealed that improvements in local transfer do not necessarily expand the overall generalization range, with some techniques enhancing local transfer but reducing far transfer. This framework offers a nuanced understanding of learning algorithms' generalization capabilities beyond traditional aggregate performance metrics.

items.title: Researchers identify cliff tokens as single-token failure triggers in LLM mathematical reasoning, introducing a taxonomy and optimization method that improves accuracy by up to 6.6 across benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified "cliff tokens" as specific single tokens in large language models (LLMs) that trigger failures in mathematical reasoning tasks. These tokens cause a significant drop in token-wise potential, marking the point where the model's output shifts from correct to incorrect. The study introduces a taxonomy categorizing cliff tokens into deterministic, uncertain, and sampled-off types, each with distinct probabilistic behaviors, and demonstrates that removing the first cliff token and resampling can substantially improve model accuracy across multiple benchmarks. The team validated their findings across seven models and three mathematical reasoning datasets, showing that optimizing model responses at uncertain and sampled-off cliff tokens using a method called Cliff-DPO leads to accuracy improvements of up to 6.6 percentage points. This approach enhances reasoning performance, while deterministic cliffs appear less responsive to optimization. The research offers a new perspective on pinpointing and addressing failure points in LLM reasoning processes, potentially guiding future improvements in model reliability and accuracy.

items.title: Researchers introduce SWE-Pro benchmark showing current LLMs fail to match expert software performance optimizations in runtime and memory across real-world codebases [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced SWE-Pro, a new benchmark designed to evaluate software performance optimization in real-world codebases. This benchmark, based on 102 expert-written optimizations from open-source projects, assesses runtime, peak memory, and Time-Weighted Memory Usage under varying conditions, addressing limitations of previous benchmarks that focused on isolated functions or single metrics. Their evaluation reveals that current Large Language Models (LLMs) perform poorly in optimizing software, showing negligible runtime improvements and almost no memory optimization compared to expert implementations. SWE-Pro incorporates parameterized tests and noise-aware measurements to capture the complex trade-offs between execution time and memory footprint, reflecting realistic development environments. Expert optimizations achieve significant gains, with an average speedup of 15.5 times and peak memory reductions of 171.3 times across tasks, improvements observed in over 90% of runtime tasks and nearly 66% of memory tasks. The findings highlight a substantial gap between the capabilities of current LLMs and the demands of expert-level software engineering.

items.title: Researchers propose SafeVec and RAS metric to evaluate LLM safety via internal refusal alignment, demonstrating faster and effective assessment across Llama, Gemma, and Qwen models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced SafeVec, a novel white-box evaluation method for assessing the safety of large language models (LLMs) by analyzing their internal representations rather than their generated outputs. This approach extracts refusal directions from a safety-aligned reference model and measures how well a target model's hidden states align with these directions when faced with unsafe or jailbreak prompts. The resulting Refusal Alignment Score (RAS) provides a calibrated safety metric ranging from 0 to 100. Testing across Llama, Gemma, and Qwen model families, RAS effectively distinguishes between aligned and uncensored or altered models, correlates with output-level attack success rates, and offers a faster alternative to traditional judge-based safety evaluations. These findings suggest that refusal alignment offers a compact and efficient signal for evaluating LLM safety from within the model's internal processes.

items.title: Researchers find reinforcement learning improves large language models' ability to navigate and recall parametric knowledge hierarchies without adding new information [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that reinforcement learning (RL) enhances large language models' (LLMs) ability to navigate and recall knowledge hierarchies within their parameters, rather than simply adding new information. Their study shows that reasoning models trained with RL outperform instruction-tuned models on knowledge recall tasks by improving procedural skills for hierarchical knowledge traversal. This improvement is supported by experiments demonstrating better recall of previously inaccessible facts and superior performance on depth-stratified retrieval tasks. Further analysis reveals that while the factual knowledge representations remain similar between models, the way queries are processed diverges, indicating that RL primarily refines the navigation process through existing knowledge. The study also notes that distilled models often fail to match reasoning models because they lack the exploratory behavior necessary for effective hierarchical navigation. These findings suggest that enhancing factual recall in LLMs depends not only on expanding their knowledge but also on teaching them to better traverse it, pointing toward future post-training methods focused on optimizing knowledge navigation.

items.title: Researchers introduce Membox, a hierarchical memory architecture for LLM agents that organizes dialogue by topic continuity, improving long-range memory retrieval and performance on LoCoMo and DialSim benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Membox, a hierarchical memory architecture designed to enhance long-range memory retrieval in large language model (LLM) agents by organizing dialogue according to topic continuity. Membox features two components: the Topic Loom, which groups dialogue turns by local topics, and the Trace Weaver, which connects events across these groups to form macro-topic traces that capture recurring goals and developments over time. This approach improves memory access by focusing on task- and topic-level continuity rather than just semantic proximity. Testing on the LoCoMo and DialSim benchmarks demonstrated significant performance gains, with Topic Loom retrieval alone increasing F1 scores by 13 points compared to previous methods, and further improvements achieved through trace-expanded retrieval. These results indicate that incorporating hierarchical topic continuity into memory systems can substantially enhance the ability of LLM agents to maintain coherent, long-term dialogues across multiple sessions.

items.title: Researchers propose approximate structured diffusion method for sequence labelling, improving POS-tagging accuracy with 16.5% error reduction using neural network-parameterized CRFs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed an approximate structured diffusion method to enhance sequence labelling in natural language processing, specifically improving part-of-speech (POS) tagging accuracy. This approach extends traditional neural network-parameterized linear-chain Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) by conditioning on entire label sequences through diffusion, addressing limitations related to finite decision spans and long-range dependencies. Experimental results demonstrate a 16.5% reduction in error rates for POS-tagging using this technique combined with approximate CRF inference. Traditional CRFs typically consider limited label dependencies, such as bigrams, which can restrict their expressiveness and performance. By introducing diffusion to train CRFs on noisy versions of full label sequences, the researchers enable the model to capture broader contextual information. This advancement offers a promising direction for improving sequence labelling tasks in machine learning and NLP applications.

items.title: Researchers present PhoneBuddy, an open-model training approach combining real and mock app environments to improve agentic phone use task success rates by up to 45% on real devices [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed PhoneBuddy, a novel training approach that combines real and mock app environments to enhance the performance of agentic phone use models. By integrating real-device interactions with a scalable mock environment called PhoneWorld, PhoneBuddy improves task success rates on real phones by up to 45%, demonstrating significant gains over traditional supervised fine-tuning and real-app reinforcement learning alone. PhoneBuddy operates by first fine-tuning models on data collected from both real and mock environments, then applying reinforcement learning across these settings. Evaluations on 150 tasks involving apps, mini-apps, and cross-app workflows show that mixed reinforcement learning yields the highest success rates, with improvements particularly notable in app and mini-app tasks. However, challenges remain in handling complex, long cross-app workflows. These findings suggest that mock-app training complements rather than replaces real-app reinforcement learning, offering a scalable and verifiable method to train phone-use agents. The approach could advance the development of more reliable general-purpose agents capable of interacting with diverse mobile applications.

items.title: Study finds large language model GatorTron-3.9B outperforms traditional ML and deep learning models in identifying heart failure risk among 12,806 cancer patients using EHR narrative features [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A study evaluated various machine learning models to identify cancer patients at risk of heart failure (HF) using electronic health records (EHRs) from 12,806 patients diagnosed with lung, breast, and colorectal cancers. The large language model GatorTron-3.9B outperformed traditional support vector machines, a Time-Aware long short-term memory (T-LSTM) model, and the transformer model BERT in predicting HF risk, achieving the highest F1 scores. The research introduced novel narrative features derived from structured medical codes, which significantly increased feature density and improved model performance. Among the cohort, 1,602 patients developed HF after cancer, highlighting the importance of accurate risk identification to enhance treatment outcomes and patient safety.

items.title: Researchers find homogeneity bias in seven open-weight LLMs robust across 5x5 temperature and top-p decoding hyperparameter grid, with consistent bias toward Hispanic and Asian Americans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified a consistent homogeneity bias in seven open-weight large language models (LLMs), where Hispanic and Asian Americans are portrayed as more internally similar compared to White Americans. This bias remains stable across a wide range of decoding hyperparameters, including temperature and top-p settings, and is evident in at least 18 of 20 configurations across six of the seven models tested. The study also found that biases related to African American and gender groups vary by model and are less robust. The analysis included a names-based approach, using racially distinctive surnames to signal group identity instead of explicit labels. This method confirmed the homogeneity bias for Hispanic and Asian groups but revealed that Black-coded surnames led to less homogeneous outputs than White-coded names, a reversal not seen in the label-based approach. These findings highlight how the way group identity is represented influences the type and direction of biases that emerge in LLM outputs.

items.title: Researchers propose SyncLoop, a multimodal dual-loop framework that jointly evolves training data and model capabilities to improve mathematical reasoning in large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced SyncLoop, a multimodal dual-loop framework designed to enhance mathematical reasoning in large language models by jointly evolving training data and model capabilities. This approach addresses challenges in existing methods that separately augment visual or textual data and evolve data and models independently, which can lead to mismatched task difficulties. SyncLoop combines a cross-modal data evolution loop that generates complex multimodal problems with a data-model evolution loop that adaptively selects problems based on model performance for iterative fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. The framework starts with a base dataset and model, expanding the dataset by integrating structured textual sub-problems with geometric diagrams while continuously refining the model through supervised and reinforcement learning. This closed-loop process results in consistent performance improvements across multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks. The researchers plan to release their code, models, and datasets to support further development in this area.

items.title: Researchers argue that deferring visual reasoning to language generation collapses spatial signals and impairs performance on visual tasks hard to verbalize, proposing reasoning within perception instead [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers challenge the common assumption in multimodal AI that stronger language reasoning can compensate for the perceptual limitations of vision-language models. They argue that deferring visual reasoning to language generation collapses critical spatial information into discrete textual representations, impairing performance on visual tasks that are difficult to verbalize. This shift from continuous visual processing to text-based reasoning reduces perception to a passive encoding step, undermining effective visual understanding. The study introduces the Turing Eye Test (TET) to demonstrate that tasks requiring reasoning within visual space cannot be adequately solved through text-only reasoning. The authors suggest rethinking AI architectures to enable reasoning directly within perception, allowing active, reasoning-driven processing of pixel-level visual data rather than relying on collapsed textual representations. This approach aims to preserve spatial signals essential for complex visual reasoning tasks.

items.title: Researchers analyze Classifier-based Quality Filtering for large-scale model pretraining, finding it improves downstream tasks by removing noise rather than enhancing high-quality data modeling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have conducted an in-depth analysis of Classifier-based Quality Filtering (CQF), a method used to improve large-scale model pretraining by filtering web-crawled datasets of mixed quality. Their study reveals that while CQF enhances performance on downstream tasks, it does not necessarily improve language modeling on high-quality data. Notably, training on CQF-selected data can outperform training directly on the high-quality dataset, even when the latter is large, suggesting that CQF effectively removes noise rather than simply identifying the best data. The researchers explain this paradox by showing that CQF implicitly filters both low- and high-quality data, refining the training set beyond just selecting high-quality documents. They also introduce an optimization-driven concept of data quality that can be reliably estimated through small-scale proxy experiments. These findings clarify the mechanisms behind CQF and contribute to a better understanding of data selection strategies commonly employed in large-scale model training.

items.title: Researchers introduce SPARC framework that separates perception and reasoning in vision-language models to improve test-time scaling and reduce compute, boosting performance on visual reasoning benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed SPARC, a new framework for vision-language models that separates visual perception from reasoning to improve test-time scaling and reduce computational demands. By implementing a two-stage process-first localizing relevant image regions through visual search, then reasoning based on those regions-SPARC allows for more efficient and targeted processing. This modular approach enhances performance on visual reasoning benchmarks while enabling flexible compute allocation and selective optimization. SPARC's design draws inspiration from the brain's sensory-to-cognitive processing and supports compressed contexts by performing global searches at lower resolutions and focusing high-resolution analysis only where needed. The framework outperforms existing models, notably improving results on the VQA benchmark and surpassing prior methods in out-of-distribution settings with significantly lower token budgets, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex visual reasoning tasks.

items.title: CLEF launches HIPE-2026 lab to evaluate person-place relation extraction from noisy multilingual historical texts with accuracy, efficiency, and domain generalization metrics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: HIPE-2026 is a CLEF evaluation lab focused on extracting person-place relations from noisy, multilingual historical texts. Building on previous HIPE campaigns, it challenges systems to identify two types of relations-whether a person has ever been at a place and whether they were located there around the publication time-requiring analysis of temporal and geographical information. The lab evaluates submissions based on accuracy, computational efficiency, and domain generalization. By advancing semantic relation extraction in historical documents, HIPE-2026 supports applications such as knowledge-graph construction, historical biography reconstruction, and spatial analysis within digital humanities. This initiative aims to enhance large-scale processing of historical data across multiple languages and time periods.

items.title: Researchers introduce MemDreamer, a framework decoupling perception and reasoning for long video understanding using hierarchical graph memory and agentic retrieval, achieving state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MemDreamer, a new framework designed to improve long video understanding by separating perception from reasoning. This approach uses a Hierarchical Graph Memory to incrementally process video content and an agentic retrieval mechanism that navigates this structure during inference. MemDreamer achieves state-of-the-art performance on four major benchmarks, significantly reducing the gap with human experts while using only a small fraction of the full video context for reasoning. The framework constructs a three-tier semantic abstraction graph capturing spatiotemporal and causal relationships, enabling efficient exploration and logical reasoning through an Observation-Reason-Action loop. Experiments demonstrate a 12.5 point accuracy improvement and highlight a strong correlation between vision-language models' logic reasoning abilities and their performance on long-video understanding tasks, suggesting agentic capability scaling as a promising direction for multimodal comprehension.

items.title: Researchers present TOTEN, a knowledge-based system preserving physical quantities and technical notation in Brazilian Portuguese, outperforming baselines in unit atomicity and numerical reconstruction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed TOTEN, a knowledge-based system designed to preserve physical quantities, numbers, units, and technical notation in Brazilian Portuguese texts. Unlike traditional tokenization methods that fragment these entities, TOTEN maintains each technical element as a whole, typed unit using a formal ontology of engineering entities. This approach improves the accuracy of AI systems that reason quantitatively over technical documents by preventing errors caused by fragmented input. TOTEN integrates deterministic links to external authorities for dimensional, typographic, and morphological consistency and was evaluated on both internal and external Brazilian Portuguese corpora. It outperformed eight state-of-the-art baselines in unit atomicity and numerical reconstruction, showing significant improvements in preserving the integrity of technical information. The system offers a reliable, auditable, and cost-effective input layer for intelligent technical knowledge processing without relying on generative models.

items.title: Researchers introduce VADAOrchestra, a neurosymbolic framework combining LLM orchestration and symbolic inference for adaptive, scalable reasoning workflows with auditability in financial use cases [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed VADAOrchestra, a neurosymbolic framework that integrates Large Language Model (LLM) orchestration with symbolic inference to create adaptive and scalable reasoning workflows. This hybrid approach models complex decision-making processes as evolving workflows, using an LLM-based orchestrator to plan and adjust actions dynamically, while encoding these workflows in a logic programming language executed by a symbolic engine. The framework aims to combine the flexibility of LLMs with the rigor and auditability of traditional symbolic systems, addressing challenges in scalability and transparency. VADAOrchestra encodes workflows as logic programs in a fragment of Datalog+/-, where predicates represent tool calls and rules capture domain dependencies and synthesized logic. This separation of high-level orchestration from symbolic inference enables efficient reasoning over large datasets through targeted queries, providing verifiable reasoning traces that support auditability and reproducibility. The framework was evaluated on real-world financial use cases, demonstrating improved faithfulness, scalability, and explainability compared to standard agentic architectures.

items.title: Researchers use large language models to automate generation of challenging benchmarks for neural relational reasoners, improving Edge Transformer generalization and enabling autonomous research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a method using large language models (LLMs) to automate the creation of challenging benchmarks for neural relational reasoners, specifically improving the Edge Transformer model's ability to generalize to harder problem instances. By employing LLM-driven evolutionary and autonomous agentic search techniques, they generate increasingly difficult problem samples based on Datalog rules, enabling systematic evaluation and enhancement of reasoning models. This approach not only improves the Edge Transformer's performance on perturbed data but also allows the generation of novel problem worlds proposed by LLMs, paving the way for autonomous research in neural relational reasoning. The method addresses the challenge of identifying and producing hard instances for testing generalization, which has traditionally hindered progress in this area.

items.title: Researchers find low-bit quantization in reasoning models preserves accuracy but increases reasoning token usage, causing hidden compute costs and longer reasoning chains across benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that low-bit post-training quantization of reasoning models, while preserving final-answer accuracy, leads to longer chains of thought during reasoning tasks. This increase in reasoning token usage offsets the expected speedup from quantization, introducing hidden compute costs across various benchmarks including mathematical reasoning, code generation, and scientific question answering. The study introduces the CoT Token Inflation Ratio to quantify this effect and observes behavioral changes such as more intermediate steps and semantic repetition in the reasoning process. The research highlights that these longer reasoning chains result in measurable real-world serving penalties despite maintained accuracy. Mitigation strategies like prompting and decoding-time sampling show inconsistent trade-offs, whereas quantization-aware training appears more effective in reducing both accuracy loss and token inflation. The findings suggest that reasoning-token usage should be reported alongside accuracy when evaluating quantized reasoning models to fully capture their performance impact.

items.title: Researchers present a multi-agent discovery engine that evolves hardware-compliant foundation model compression methods, deploying a 235-billion-parameter model on constrained dual-A100 servers with 75% memory reduction and minimal accuracy loss [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a multi-agent discovery engine that autonomously designs hardware-compliant computing systems by leveraging an Evolutionary Knowledge Graph to guide structural evolution. This engine created two hardware-aware compression methods that outperform existing human-engineered techniques, enabling the deployment of a 235-billion-parameter foundation model on limited dual-A100 servers with a 75% reduction in memory usage and only a 0.64% drop in accuracy. The framework addresses the challenge of hardware incompatibility in AI model design by transforming random search processes into directed, knowledge-driven evolution. Its compression methods, Q-Enhance and MoE-Salient-AQ, improve accuracy retention in dense models and surpass state-of-the-art sparse Mixture-of-Experts designs, respectively. This approach demonstrates a scalable hardware-software co-design paradigm for machine-driven discovery within strict physical constraints.

items.title: Researchers release WinDOM, a 54,425-record GUI grounding corpus and Self-Family Distillation method to improve small-model GUI agents without human annotation or external teachers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced WinDOM, a GUI grounding corpus containing 54,425 records, and a Self-Family Distillation (SFD) method designed to enhance the performance of small-scale GUI agents without relying on human annotation or external teacher models. WinDOM was created by automatically extracting bounding box data from an open-source Windows 11 web implementation using headless Playwright, eliminating the need for OCR or manual labeling. The SFD approach uses either an exponential moving average of the student model or a frozen larger teacher model from the same family to guide training, optimizing reinforcement learning initialization. The study demonstrates that using an under-saturated cold-start in SFD provides better reinforcement learning initialization than a fully converged model, resulting in significant performance gains on out-of-distribution benchmarks. Notably, the same-size EMA variant achieves nearly comparable results to the larger teacher model without external supervision, highlighting the method's effectiveness for improving small-model GUI agents while maintaining efficiency and reducing annotation costs.

items.title: Researchers introduce InvestPhilBench, a multi-layer dynamic benchmark with 243 questions to evaluate large language models' procedural reasoning in expert investment philosophy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed InvestPhilBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability to replicate and apply expert investment decision-making processes. This multi-layer dynamic benchmark includes 243 questions across eight cognitive levels, supported by verified investment principles and decision frameworks. It introduces an automated scoring system with multiple metrics to assess model performance and identify failure modes. The current version, v0.6, serves primarily as a methodological tool, featuring a unified evaluation approach and model-in-the-loop retrieval conditions. Initial testing on several models revealed a notable gap between overall scoring and procedural reasoning accuracy, indicating that while models can produce fluent responses, they still struggle with the underlying decision frameworks. Future releases aim to provide a de-confounded leaderboard and expanded evaluation conditions to further refine assessment of procedural reasoning in investment contexts.

items.title: Researchers present the Unfireable Safety Kernel, a Rust-based execution-time AI alignment system for escapable AI agents, verified by formal methods and tested against self-modifying adversaries [ ~ ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed the Unfireable Safety Kernel, a Rust-based execution-time AI alignment system designed to control escapable AI agents that can influence their own runtime environment. This system enforces strict architectural controls through process separation, pre-action enforcement, fail-closed mechanisms, and external verification, aiming to complement existing training-time and inference-time alignment methods. The kernel's fail-closed properties have been rigorously verified using formal methods, including SMT theorem proving and bounded model checking. The Unfireable Safety Kernel was tested on a live, self-improving AI system against adversarial attempts to bypass safety controls. Across 1,000 self-modifications, all 704 attempts to alter the safety-critical core were blocked, and additional operator interventions prevented further unauthorized changes. Extensive authorization checks showed no successful bypasses, demonstrating the kernel's robustness in maintaining control over AI agents that might otherwise escape traditional runtime constraints. This development represents a significant step toward reliable execution-time AI alignment, providing a verified safety layer that prevents AI agents from circumventing controls embedded within their own runtime. By externalizing control verification and enforcing strict fail-closed policies, the Unfireable Safety Kernel offers a promising approach to managing advanced AI systems with self-modifying capabilities.

items.title: Researchers identify readout blind spot in looped language models where dense supervision controls only exposed variables, proposing scale-visible readouts and norm penalties to improve recurrent scale control and reduce perplexity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified a limitation in looped language models where dense supervision via cross-entropy loss only controls the variables exposed by the readout, not all variables active in the recurrent transition. This creates a blind spot in controlling hidden-state scale, especially with scale-invariant readouts like RMSNorm and LayerNorm, which mask scale from the loss while it continues to evolve in the recurrence. As a result, hidden-state norms can grow excessively large without being regulated by the loss. The study demonstrates that using scale-visible readouts and explicit norm penalties can keep hidden-state norms within reasonable bounds, while architectural changes that remove scale from the recurrence complement this approach. Experiments with looped transformers show that models incorporating these scale control methods achieve lower perplexity at comparable inference depths. The findings suggest a design principle: dense supervision effectively trains prediction exits, but controlling recurrent scale requires either making scale visible to the loss or eliminating it from the loop.

items.title: Researchers report human-AI co-discovery of sign-embedding quantum algorithms for matrix equations and functions, highlighting AI's role in problem formation and theorem development [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated a human-AI collaborative approach to discovering sign-embedding quantum algorithms for matrix equations and functions, which are key components in quantum linear algebra. The project began with a human intuition about the effectiveness of rational approximation for certain functions and used AI-assisted exploration, including the AIM system, to develop this idea into a concrete framework and extend it to broader classes of problems. While AI contributed to formulating routes, comparing options, and drafting proofs, critical scientific decisions and refinements were made by human researchers. This study highlights the value of AI not just as a tool for solving fixed problems but as a partner in the early stages of mathematical research, helping to shape problem formation, discover connections, and support derivations within a human-guided process. The findings suggest that human-AI co-discovery workflows can enhance the development of new mathematical theories by combining computational assistance with human judgment and skepticism.

items.title: Researchers propose lightweight on-device Neural Architecture Search for real-time sensor data analysis, validated on Italian Sign Language and fault diagnosis datasets with improved accuracy and lower RAM use on Raspberry Pi 4 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a lightweight Neural Architecture Search (NAS) method that operates directly on deployment devices to optimize tiny neural networks for real-time sensor data analysis. This approach is particularly beneficial for human-machine interfaces, allowing neural networks to be reconfigured for different users after a guided data collection process, addressing individual data variability. The method was validated on the Italian Sign Language dataset using surface electromyography signals and on a fault diagnosis benchmark dataset, demonstrating improved accuracy and reduced memory usage on embedded systems like the Raspberry Pi 4. The proposed NAS achieved a 5.96 percentage point increase in accuracy with 37% less RAM usage on the Italian Sign Language dataset and a 0.2 percentage point accuracy improvement with 56% less RAM usage on the fault diagnosis dataset. These results suggest the approach's potential for efficient, adaptive on-device learning in various sensor-based applications.

items.title: arXiv: Industrial Continual Learning for LLMs framed as a versioned update-and-release ecosystem addressing model plasticity, capability inheritance, and deployment sustainability challenges [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A new survey on Industrial Continual Learning (ICL) for large language models (LLMs) presents a versioned update-and-release ecosystem to address challenges in model adaptation, capability inheritance, and deployment sustainability. The study frames ICL as a closed-loop process where updates propagate through hierarchical model versions, highlighting issues such as loss of model plasticity, disruptions from foundation-model upgrades, and constraints from deployment demands. The authors organize the technical landscape around five design principles: preserving plasticity, treating upgrades as capability transfer, enabling trustworthy continual reinforcement learning, self-optimizing training recipes, and embedding accountability for long-term iteration. They assess the maturity of these principles, identify gaps hindering real-world application, and propose a practical deployment blueprint to align industrial needs with academic research.

items.title: Researchers propose Recursive Quantum LSTM with dynamic variational quantum circuit adaptation for improved sequential data processing and temporal information propagation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced a Recursive Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (Recursive QLSTM) model that enhances quantum sequential data processing by incorporating metacore-based recursive structures. This model extends previous QLSTM designs and has been tested across various input sequence lengths, metacore configurations, and recursive rules to identify the most effective architecture. The study provides theoretical insights into how the recursive design improves temporal information flow and learning efficiency. The Recursive QLSTM framework demonstrates flexibility and improved performance in quantum recurrent learning tasks involving time series data of different lengths. These findings suggest that recursive structures in quantum models can offer significant advantages for processing sequential information in quantum machine learning applications.

items.title: Researchers propose Self-Modulating Quantum Fast Weight Programmers to improve convergence and prediction in quantum machine learning for sequential data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Self-Modulating Quantum Fast Weight Programmers (Self-Modulating QFWP), an advancement in quantum machine learning designed to enhance sequential data processing. This approach builds on existing Quantum Fast Weight Programmers by incorporating adaptive modulation of both new fast-weight updates and historical memory, leading to improved convergence stability and prediction accuracy across various model configurations. The study presents numerical evidence supporting the effectiveness of Self-Modulating QFWP with different numbers of qubits and input sequence lengths. Theoretical analysis explains that the self-modulation mechanism optimally balances the integration of new information with the retention of past data, thereby improving the propagation of temporal information. These findings suggest that Self-Modulating QFWP offers a compact and efficient framework for quantum machine learning applications involving time-series data.

items.title: Researchers present Stable-Shift, a biologically structured method predicting transcriptional responses to unseen gene perturbations using graph convolution and biological context integration [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Stable-Shift, a novel method designed to predict transcriptional responses to gene perturbations that have not been previously observed during training. This approach aggregates single-cell data into expression shifts at the perturbation level, fits a low-rank response basis from known perturbations, and predicts responses for unseen genes by integrating biological context such as protein interactions, network structure, expression statistics, and gene annotations using graph convolution. Tested on the K562 Perturb-seq benchmark, Stable-Shift outperformed existing methods like GEARS, achieving higher cosine similarity, Spearman correlation, and precision in identifying top genes. The method demonstrated consistent performance across multiple datasets and gene splits, supporting the potential of biologically structured latent-response prediction. However, limitations remain due to lower accuracy in gene-space predictions and sensitivity to sparse network data, indicating areas for further research and refinement.

items.title: Researchers study holographic memory models for zero-shot compositional reasoning in knowledge graphs, finding failures due to retrieval capacity limits and interference effects [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers investigated holographic memory models, specifically real-valued Holographic Reduced Representations (HRR) and phase-only Fourier HRR (FHRR), to assess their ability to perform zero-shot compositional reasoning in knowledge graphs. While both models performed well on single-hop link predictions, they failed to accurately handle multi-hop queries involving relation chains not seen during training. The study identified that the failure was not due to the binding and unbinding operations or cleanup mechanisms but stemmed from intrinsic retrieval capacity limits and interference effects when facts are superposed in memory. The team conducted detailed probes revealing that although the models could retrieve intermediate entities with high accuracy, composing these into multi-hop answers remained unsuccessful. Additionally, they found that the softmax cleanup in FHRR was not phase-equivariant, which exacerbated errors in some cases. The findings suggest that improving zero-shot compositional reasoning will require enhancing retrieval capacity under superposition rather than merely redesigning cleanup processes.

items.title: Researchers release MacroLens, a multi-task benchmark for contextual financial reasoning using prices, accounting data, macroeconomic series, SEC filings, and news for 4,416 US small- and micro-cap equities from 2021 to 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced MacroLens, a comprehensive multi-task benchmark designed for contextual financial reasoning that integrates price data, accounting fundamentals, macroeconomic indicators, SEC filings, and news articles. Covering 4,416 U.S. small- and micro-cap equities from 2021 to 2026, MacroLens addresses challenges in financial time-series evaluation by incorporating seven tasks that utilize a unified dataset including prices, 46.8 million accounting facts, 53 macroeconomic series, nearly 300,000 SEC filings, and over 215,000 news articles, alongside a scenario layer of macroeconomic events rendered in natural language. The benchmark evaluates 19 methods across six categories, ranging from simple heuristics to advanced time-series foundation models and large language models (LLMs), including fine-tuned and zero-shot approaches. It also features a detailed ablation study on feature context using leading LLMs and a gradient-boosted baseline. MacroLens aims to facilitate more accurate and context-aware financial decision-making by providing a publicly available, integrated dataset and evaluation framework, which is accessible at https://huggingface.co/datasets/DeepAuto-AI/MacroLens.

items.title: Researchers propose DCQ-GNN, a spectral graph neural network using convex-concave quadratic filters to improve spectral selectivity and robustness on heterophilic and homophilic graphs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced DCQ-GNN, a spectral graph neural network that uses a compact set of adaptive convex-concave quadratic filters to enhance spectral selectivity and robustness on both heterophilic and homophilic graphs. By limiting the filter order to two and leveraging complementary curvature, DCQ-GNN achieves improved frequency filtering without the complexity of high-order polynomial expansions. The model incorporates a node-adaptive gating mechanism for structure-aware spectral selection, enabling efficient and stable optimization. The team conducted a formal spectral analysis based on Dirichlet energy attenuation, von Neumann entropy, and curvature polarity, characterizing filter behavior under varying graph homophily and structural perturbations. Benchmarking on ten datasets showed that DCQ-GNN ranks among the top performers on heterophilic graphs and is competitive on homophilic graphs, outperforming many existing spectral filters. Additionally, DCQ-GNN demonstrated greater resilience to structural perturbations compared to both first-order and high-order spectral models, highlighting its robustness and computational efficiency as an alternative approach in graph neural network design.

items.title: Researchers introduce a conformal prediction method for ordinal classification using ranked probability score, offering contiguous prediction sets and improved uncertainty quantification across image and tabular datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a new conformal prediction method for ordinal classification that utilizes the ranked probability score (RPS) to generate contiguous prediction sets with reliable uncertainty quantification. This approach is particularly relevant for high-stakes fields like medicine and finance, where the severity of ordinal errors must be carefully considered. The method is model-agnostic, supports various types of ordered categorical outcomes, and offers efficient implementation compared to existing techniques. By using RPS as the nonconformity measure, the method produces median-centered prediction sets that balance prediction set width and the magnitude of ordinal miscoverage effectively. Tests on multiple ordinal image and tabular datasets demonstrate that this RPS-based conformal prediction approach outperforms traditional methods by providing more coherent and reliable uncertainty estimates in ordinal classification tasks.

items.title: Researchers present xAARA, an uncertainty-aware multi-expert fusion system that achieves 94.2% task accuracy in stroke rehabilitation assessment and reduces predictive uncertainty by 96.1% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed xAARA, an uncertainty-aware multi-expert fusion system designed to enhance stroke rehabilitation assessment by providing detailed evaluations of movement quality rather than just success. Using multi-view video and a Dynamic Bayesian Network, xAARA integrates 692 calibrated multimodal models to deliver Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) scores with calibrated uncertainty and explanations, achieving 94.2% task accuracy and significantly reducing predictive uncertainty compared to traditional single-clinician scoring. Tested on 105 stroke survivors performing 788 exercises, xAARA demonstrated high agreement with clinical raters and deferred low-confidence cases to ensure reliability. Independent clinicians validated the system's assessments and expressed willingness to adopt it, highlighting its potential to augment clinical judgment. The researchers emphasize that combining principled uncertainty quantification with clinician-aligned explainability is key to transitioning automated assessment tools from research prototypes to practical clinical applications.

items.title: Researchers find language priors reduce reconstruction error by 81% in learned Darcy-flow inverse solvers using sentence embeddings for geological descriptions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated that incorporating language priors through sentence embeddings significantly improves the accuracy of learned Darcy-flow inverse solvers used in geological modeling. By injecting qualitative geological descriptions as text conditioning, they achieved an 81% reduction in reconstruction error compared to models without text input. This approach was tested across six synthetic geological classes and a benchmark reservoir model, highlighting the effectiveness of language-based constraints in underdetermined regions of the conductivity field. The study found that most of the improvement stems from class-level categorical constraints, while finer geometric details within classes had a smaller, pattern-dependent impact. Compared to using discrete class labels, sentence embeddings offered enhanced training stability and enabled sensitivity analyses based on paraphrases and open-vocabulary inputs. These findings suggest that language priors can serve as a valuable interface for integrating qualitative engineering knowledge into inverse solvers, clarifying their role and the nature of the information they convey.

items.title: Researchers propose spectral entropy to quantify signal noise introduced by explainable AI in ECG arrhythmia classification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have proposed using spectral entropy as a metric to quantify the signal noise introduced by explainable AI (XAI) techniques in deep learning models, particularly in healthcare applications. Their study focuses on the challenge of distinguishing between the true signal from the model and noise added by XAI heuristics when interpreting model outputs. They demonstrate the effectiveness of spectral entropy in measuring noise within explanations generated for classifying arrhythmias in ECG data using various post hoc explainability methods. This approach addresses the critical need for trustworthy and justifiable AI decisions in medical contexts, where understanding the reliability of explanations is essential. By applying spectral entropy, the researchers provide a quantitative tool to evaluate the clarity and fidelity of XAI outputs, potentially improving the interpretability and acceptance of AI-driven diagnostic tools.

items.title: Researchers propose retrieval-augmented personalization using foundation models for wearable stress detection, improving accuracy by nearly 4% on WESAD dataset without labeled user data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a retrieval-augmented personalization method using foundation models to improve wearable stress detection. This approach enhances accuracy by nearly 4% on the WESAD dataset without requiring any labeled user data, addressing the challenge of individual variability in physiological and behavioral responses. The method uses frozen foundation models to retrieve similar patterns from a user's history and creates personalized embeddings that improve stress detection performance with a lightweight transformer network. Tested on data from 15 users wearing wrist devices measuring physiological signals and activity, the method outperformed non-personalized baselines and approached the accuracy of supervised fine-tuning. It also demonstrated robustness when only prior user samples were available and showed potential for cross-dataset personalization by leveraging embeddings from a different dataset to enhance stress detection on WESAD.

items.title: Researchers find multimodal sensor fusion reduces robustness in automated cattle posture classification under temporal distribution shifts across 2024-2025 data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers evaluated the robustness of automated cattle posture classification systems using multimodal sensor data, including collar accelerometers, rumen-bolus sensors, and environmental measurements collected from a beef cattle herd over two years (2024-2025). While models combining multiple sensor types showed high accuracy within the same year, their performance dropped significantly when tested on data from a different year, indicating reduced robustness under temporal distribution shifts. The study found that reliance on certain sensor signals persisted even as predictive accuracy declined, suggesting that multimodal fusion may not always enhance generalization in real-world conditions. The research employed various machine learning models, including XGBoost, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Long Short-Term Memory networks, and assessed model performance using increasingly stringent validation methods, such as leave-one-animal-out and cross-year evaluations. Analysis revealed substantial differences in feature distributions between years, which contributed to the decline in model performance. These findings highlight that standard evaluation protocols may overestimate the readiness of such systems for deployment and emphasize the importance of robustness-focused assessments in livestock monitoring applications.

items.title: Researchers propose uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning methods for chemical language models to improve molecular design reliability and increase true hit rates by 25% [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning (RL) methods for Chemical Language Models (CLMs) to enhance the reliability of molecular design. Traditional RL approaches treat scoring functions as deterministic, ignoring prediction uncertainties that can lead to unstable optimization and unreliable molecule generation. The new methods incorporate uncertainty either as an additional optimization objective or by modulating policy updates to reduce the influence of uncertain predictions, enabling more robust exploration of chemical space. These approaches were tested in controlled and real-world settings using ChemProp models and a Conformal Prediction wrapper on a Random Forest classifier. Results showed that uncertainty-aware RL favors lower-uncertainty regions, improving the true hit rate by 25% (from 50% to 75%) and nearly doubling the total number of true hits without compromising molecular scores. This advancement promises more dependable hit discovery in molecular design applications.

items.title: Researchers introduce ExTra, a trajectory optimization framework that improves language model reinforcement learning accuracy by adding exploration signals and diversity rewards across six reasoning benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed ExTra, a new trajectory optimization framework designed to enhance reinforcement learning for language models by incorporating exploration signals and diversity rewards. This approach addresses challenges in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), where easy tasks yield low-diversity, all-correct outputs with limited learning signals, and difficult tasks produce mostly incorrect results with no positive feedback. ExTra introduces a novelty reward to encourage diverse correct solutions and uses entropy-guided prefix regeneration to explore promising partial trajectories. Tested across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, ExTra demonstrated significant improvements over existing methods, increasing accuracy by approximately 5 points on pass@1 and 7 points on pass@16 for the Qwen3-1.7B model. These results suggest that leveraging trajectory-level exploration signals can effectively boost both single-sample accuracy and inference-time coverage in language model reasoning tasks.

items.title: Researchers evaluate robustness of tabular foundation models to biologically inspired distribution shifts in six gut microbiome datasets across four disease contexts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have assessed the robustness of tabular foundation models (TFMs) when applied to gut microbiome data across six datasets and four disease contexts, focusing on their performance under biologically inspired distribution shifts. The study introduced a benchmark where models were tested on perturbed query samples while using unaltered support sets as context, applying three types of controlled perturbations: removal of high-abundance taxa, increased zero-inflation (sparsification), and zero-imputation through spurious non-zero injections. The findings reveal that even when key discriminative taxa are preserved, all perturbations degrade model performance, with zero-imputation causing the most significant harm, indicating that disrupting global feature structure undermines generalization. The study also found that TFMs are more sensitive to sparsification compared to classical random forest models, suggesting a particular vulnerability to zero-inflation-type shifts. These results highlight limitations in the stability of TFMs under realistic distribution changes in microbiome data, emphasizing the need for further research to improve their robustness. The code for this benchmark is publicly available for further exploration and validation.

items.title: Researchers find internal data repetition in training corpora systematically damages language model performance, quantifying compute-equivalent loss under Chinchilla scaling laws [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that internal repetition within training data systematically harms the performance of language models, even when datasets are aggressively deduplicated. Using updated Chinchilla-style scaling laws, they quantified the compute-equivalent loss caused by repeated data and identified that performance degradation peaks at an intermediate level of repetition. This effect is influenced by model size and the structure of repeated data, with moderate repetition of a moderately sized subset causing more damage than other repetition patterns. The study demonstrates that when repeated documents consume a significant portion of the computational budget, the resulting loss can be equivalent to reducing compute by a large margin. These findings are supported by a simple statistical model showing a tradeoff between memorization and generalization. This work provides a precise framework for understanding and quantifying the wasted computational resources due to duplication in language model pretraining corpora, offering valuable insights for practitioners aiming to optimize training efficiency.

items.title: Researchers present Geo-Strat-RL, a synthetic environment using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to improve geological event reasoning and reconstruction across stratigraphic and seismic observation domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Geo-Strat-RL, a synthetic environment designed to improve geological event reasoning and reconstruction by using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). This environment generates stratigraphic observations alongside compact event histories, allowing vision-language models to learn and verify geological processes such as chronology, event identity, deposition, and structural relationships. The approach aims to address challenges in teaching models to produce valid geological reconstructions consistent with observed evidence and geological principles. The study demonstrates that RLVR enhances geological reconstruction accuracy in vision-language models, as shown by improved scores on stratigraphic diagrams. Additionally, the learned geological reasoning transfers effectively to a synthetic seismic observation domain without requiring seismic-specific training, suggesting that RLVR can teach reusable geological reasoning concepts across different observation formats.

items.title: Researchers find standard output-level evaluation overestimates machine unlearning success, revealing residual representation mismatches compared to retrained models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that standard output-level evaluations of machine unlearning (MU) tend to overestimate its success by focusing on output forgetting metrics like low forget-set accuracy or reduced membership inference. Their study compares unlearning methods to retrained models that exclude the forget data, revealing that while output layers may appear to have forgotten, residual mismatches persist in the representation space, indicating incomplete forgetting. The analysis shows that these residual discrepancies are structured, with asymmetries between forget and retain samples and concentrated differences along retraining-related directions rather than being diffuse. This suggests that current MU evaluations often certify apparent forgetting at the output level rather than true retraining-consistent forgetting, highlighting the importance of considering representation-level consistency to accurately assess unlearning effectiveness.

items.title: Researchers introduce ADOWIP, a budgeted decision-loss priority framework for delayed online time-series adaptation with proven feasibility and improved performance on capacity-planning tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed ADOWIP, a new framework designed to optimize online time-series forecasting by deciding when to update models rather than updating at every opportunity. ADOWIP uses a decision-loss priority gate that triggers updates only after feedback is received and when the predicted loss exceeds a calibrated threshold, all while respecting computational budget constraints. The framework includes sealed delay queues, precise budget tracking, and transparent update telemetry, ensuring efficient and auditable adaptation. The team demonstrated ADOWIP's effectiveness on public capacity-planning tasks, where it reduced decision loss compared to traditional update strategies under equal computational resources. Additional tests on external datasets, such as bike-sharing capacity proxies and station rebalancing, showed consistent improvements. However, experiments in probe-based and financial domains did not yield positive results, indicating the current limitations of decision-prioritized adaptation methods.

items.title: Researchers propose GCT-MARL, a graph-based contrastive transfer learning framework that accelerates sample-efficient cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning across varying population sizes and compositions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced GCT-MARL, a graph-based contrastive transfer learning framework designed to improve sample efficiency in cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). This framework enhances the multi-view graph contrastive backbone of MAIL by incorporating an adaptively weighted alignment loss and a two-phase training protocol, enabling effective transfer learning across populations with varying sizes and compositions. The approach significantly accelerates convergence on new tasks compared to training from scratch, supporting both homogeneous and heterogeneous transfer scenarios. The framework also facilitates continual learning by applying its two-phase transfer protocol sequentially across related tasks. This unified method addresses key limitations in existing MARL transfer techniques, offering new methodological and empirical insights that could streamline deployment and reduce training costs in multi-agent systems.

items.title: Researchers propose PACE optimizer to improve iterate-averaged language model training, showing gains over AdamW in fine-tuning 1-2B parameter models and GPT-2 pretraining [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced PACE, a new optimization method designed to enhance the training of language models by focusing on the averaged model returned during training rather than the final iterate. PACE acts as a lightweight wrapper around the AdamW optimizer, guiding model weights toward their exponential moving average with controlled adjustments. This approach is grounded in an optimal-control framework that aims to minimize the error of the averaged model. The team demonstrated that PACE converges at a standard rate for stochastic convex optimization and can significantly reduce the limiting squared error in certain scenarios. Empirical tests showed that PACE outperforms both AdamW and its exponential moving average variant in fine-tuning language models with 1-2 billion parameters and in pretraining GPT-2 on the FineWeb dataset across various learning rates and hyperparameters. These findings suggest that optimizing for the iterate-averaged model can lead to improved performance in large-scale language model training, offering a promising direction for future research and practical applications in natural language processing.

items.title: Researchers present AeroCast, a Transformer-MDN model for probabilistic 3D trajectory prediction of non-cooperative aerial obstacles, halving displacement errors over five seconds and enabling real-time 100Hz inference [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed AeroCast, a probabilistic 3D trajectory prediction model designed for non-cooperative aerial obstacles such as birds, uncontrolled drones, and debris. By combining a Transformer encoder with a Mixture Density Network, AeroCast predicts Gaussian mixture distributions of future displacements, significantly improving prediction accuracy and reducing displacement errors by about 50% over a five-second horizon compared to existing methods. The model supports real-time inference at 100Hz, making it suitable for onboard deployment in autonomous aerial vehicles. AeroCast addresses challenges in modeling multi-modal motion by using a translation-invariant displacement encoding and a calibration-focused training objective. Tested on a dataset combining real and synthetic quadrotor data across nine motion categories, it achieved the lowest negative log-likelihood and Continuous Ranked Probability Score among evaluated approaches. Key factors contributing to its performance include velocity input, model capacity, and positional encoding, which ensures trajectory coherence over longer time frames.

items.title: Researchers analyze how reward design influences attention patterns in reinforcement learning agents for autonomous driving using Waymo dataset scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers examined how different reward designs influence the attention patterns of reinforcement learning agents trained for autonomous driving. Using three agents with identical architectures and training data but varying reward configurations, they analyzed attention allocation across 50 real-world scenarios from the Waymo Open Motion Dataset. Their study found that reward design significantly affects which scene elements the agents prioritize, with navigation rewards increasing focus on GPS-path tokens and continuous time-to-collision penalties fostering sustained vigilance during collision-free phases. The researchers identified that naive pooling of timesteps underestimates the relationship between attention and collision risk, recommending within-episode correlation with Fisher z-transform aggregation as a more accurate method. They also observed that agents with different reward structures can exhibit opposite attention-risk correlation directions, indicating that reward design can qualitatively change attentional strategies rather than just modulate their intensity. These findings suggest that analyzing attention patterns can serve as a practical diagnostic tool to verify that reward functions produce the intended representational behavior in safety-critical reinforcement learning systems, potentially improving the reliability and safety of autonomous driving agents.

items.title: Researchers benchmark Earth observation data-quality metrics against human judgment and land-cover segmentation performance, finding misalignment and unreliability of ImageNet-based metrics for geospatial data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have evaluated the effectiveness of common data-quality metrics used to assess synthetic Earth observation images by comparing them against human judgment and the performance of land-cover segmentation models. Their study reveals a significant misalignment: metrics like FID, which are based on ImageNet-pretrained features, often fail to reflect human perception and downstream task utility, especially when images undergo semantics-preserving changes such as rotation. Synthetic images that score poorly on these metrics can still appear realistic to humans and improve model performance when combined with real data. The team systematically tested Earth observation datasets and their synthetic counterparts generated by deep generative models, finding that automatic fidelity metrics are unreliable indicators of quality for geospatial data. Their results suggest that evaluating synthetic datasets should prioritize downstream task outcomes and human evaluation rather than relying solely on traditional visual fidelity metrics.

items.title: TokenMinds extends PLUM framework to generate pretrained Semantic ID-based user tokens and dense embeddings for large-scale recommender systems, validated on billions of YouTube users [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: TokenMinds is an industrial-scale system that enhances user modeling in large recommender systems by generating both discrete Semantic ID (SID)-based user tokens and dense user embeddings. Building on the PLUM framework and leveraging pre-trained large language models, TokenMinds combines the benefits of semantically grounded discrete representations with compatibility for existing embedding-based models. This approach addresses limitations of traditional dense embeddings and text-based user tokens by capturing richer user behavior and improving generalization. The system unifies long-form and short-form video behaviors using a shared SID vocabulary, reducing training and serving costs. TokenMinds has been validated through extensive offline experiments and live deployments on multiple YouTube platforms, handling billions of users via an asynchronous infrastructure. Results demonstrate that SID-based user tokens are practical at industrial scale and that combining tokens with dense embeddings enhances performance across various production ranking systems.

items.title: Researchers show physics-informed neural networks can produce low-loss but inaccurate solutions due to parameter poisoning, revealing limits of loss-based validation across multiple PDE systems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified a critical limitation in physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), which are designed to solve partial differential equations by embedding governing equations into their loss functions. Their study reveals that PINNs can achieve low training loss yet produce inaccurate solutions when the underlying physics parameters are perturbed, a phenomenon termed physics parameter poisoning. This challenges the common assumption that low residual loss indicates physically correct solutions. The team tested this issue across three different PDE systems-Burgers equation, Navier-Stokes cavity, and convection-diffusion-and found that poisoned models often matched or outperformed clean models in training loss while deviating significantly in solution accuracy. They introduced a detection difficulty ratio to measure how subtle these inaccuracies are and evaluated six potential defenses, none of which consistently detected the corruption. To address this, they proposed a post-hoc method that scans PDE residual loss across parameter values without retraining, successfully recovering true parameters and generalizing across systems and network architectures.

items.title: Researchers introduce ATMA, a hybrid convolutional-attention model with Polar Attention and gated-delta compression memory, achieving over 90% retrieval accuracy on 64K-token sequences and improved perplexity beyond 2K training length [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed ATMA, a hybrid convolutional-attention model that addresses limitations in long-context language modeling by combining a novel three-channel attention mechanism with a gated-delta compression memory. This approach overcomes challenges of softmax attention dilution and balances local and global context representation, enabling improved performance on extended sequences. ATMA integrates a Polar Attention core with a recurrent compression memory, allowing it to maintain over 90% retrieval accuracy on sequences up to 64,000 tokens-32 times longer than its training length of 2,000 tokens-while continuously reducing perplexity. Evaluations demonstrate that this combined model outperforms traditional softmax-based memory methods, which tend to fail at extreme context lengths.

items.title: Researchers present a Hybrid CNN-LSTM intrusion detection system for smart renewable energy grids achieving 98.2% precision and real-time inference on resource-constrained devices [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a Hybrid CNN-LSTM intrusion detection system (IDS) designed to enhance cybersecurity in smart renewable energy grids. This system combines convolutional neural networks for spatial feature extraction with long short-term memory networks for temporal sequence modeling, enabling it to detect both immediate volumetric anomalies and slow, evolving cyberattacks in real time. The model achieved a precision of 98.2% on the NSL-KDD dataset, outperforming other methods such as LSTM, CNN, Random Forest, and SVM, and demonstrated effective performance on resource-constrained devices with low latency and high throughput.

items.title: Researchers propose Future Decomposition Network for interpretable spatiotemporal forecasting with competitive accuracy and lower memory and runtime costs across hydrologic, traffic, and energy datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced the Future Decomposition Network (FDN), a new model designed for interpretable spatiotemporal forecasting. FDN offers interpretable predictions by classifying future states, uncovers hidden activity patterns in time-series data, and achieves forecasting accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art methods while using significantly less memory and runtime. The model has been tested across diverse datasets from hydrologic, traffic, and energy systems, demonstrating both improved accuracy and enhanced interpretability. FDN addresses the challenge of forecasting in complex spatiotemporal systems, where multiple interdependent entities generate dynamic signals. Unlike many recent sophisticated forecasting methods that prioritize accuracy over interpretability, FDN balances both, providing insights into the underlying patterns driving the data. Its efficiency in computational resources makes it a practical option for real-world applications requiring timely and understandable forecasts.

items.title: Researchers propose task-oriented randomization to stabilize black-box algorithms across diverse input structures, extending framework to top-k ranking and validating with simulations and real-world data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a task-oriented randomization approach to enhance the stability of black-box algorithms across diverse input types, including both structured and unstructured data. This method adapts to the underlying data generation processes and provides theoretical guarantees for stability while balancing the trade-off between stability and exploration. The framework is further extended to address top-k ranking problems, inspired by the design of Large Language Models. The study includes extensive numerical simulations and real-world data applications to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. By tailoring randomization strategies to the specific characteristics of input data, the research offers a robust solution for stabilizing outputs of black-box models, which is crucial for advancing trustworthy artificial intelligence.

items.title: Researchers present UC-Search, a risk-aware test-time search method for delayed constrained time-series control, showing positive results on multiple delayed-control and inventory validation benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced UC-Search, a model-agnostic test-time search method designed for delayed constrained time-series control under uncertainty. UC-Search integrates forecasts or action scores from a backbone model with a feasibility automaton to evaluate candidate paths, using bounded search to select the first action of a risk-adjusted feasible trajectory. The approach incorporates various uncertainty types as path-risk terms and demonstrates improved performance on multiple delayed-control and inventory management benchmarks compared to existing methods like CEM, MPPI, and risk-aware random strategies. The method was evaluated on a public suite of delayed-control tasks and inventory validation datasets, showing consistent positive results in both normalized and compute-matched audits. Additional tests on standard periodic-review lost-sales inventory and other control scenarios further support UC-Search's effectiveness. While the study reports boundary and mechanism evidence from various controls and synthetic tests, it does not claim broad dominance, highlighting the nuanced benefits of the approach in specific delayed decision-making contexts.

items.title: Researchers propose Elastic Post-Training Sparsity (EPTS) for large language model compression, enabling multi-sparsity optimization in one shot with competitive performance on LLaMA and OPT models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Elastic Post-Training Sparsity (EPTS), a new framework designed to compress large language models efficiently by enabling multi-sparsity optimization in a single process. Unlike traditional methods that require separate optimization for each sparsity level, EPTS produces a single adaptable model that maintains strong performance across various sparsity configurations, facilitating flexible deployment on different hardware. EPTS incorporates a Multi-Sparsity Hierarchy LoRA (MS-HiLoRA) mechanism to transfer knowledge from low to high sparsity groups and a Multi-Sparsity Feature Mixer (MSFM) to improve the model's resilience to pruning changes.
