Experiments on LLaMA and OPT model families show that EPTS matches or exceeds the performance of leading methods like SparseGPT and Wanda, while offering greater efficiency by supporting multiple deployment scenarios from one optimization.

items.title: Researchers propose Communicability-Inspired Positional Encoding (CIPE) for Transformers, improving graph positional encoding accuracy by 35.5% across seven benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Communicability-Inspired Positional Encoding (CIPE), a new method designed to improve positional encodings for Transformers working with non-Euclidean graph data. CIPE leverages communicability, a measure that captures multi-path connectivity between nodes, to create an attention-compatible geometry that enhances the self-attention mechanism in Transformers. This approach significantly boosts performance, improving structure-agnostic Transformers by an average of 35.5% across seven benchmarks and also enhancing structure-biased graph Transformers where other positional encodings offer limited gains. CIPE achieves this by converting global graph connectivity into a similarity geometry suitable for attention mechanisms, and includes a dimensionality alignment technique to maintain consistent representation sizes during training. The method provides a principled framework for graph positional encodings that better reflect meaningful structural relationships, positioning it as a valuable advancement in graph-based Transformer models.

items.title: Researchers present a unified framework for compositional behavioral semantics in reinforcement learning to analyze and transfer state abstractions with soundness guarantees [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a unified framework for compositional behavioral semantics in reinforcement learning, aimed at improving state abstraction in complex systems. This framework allows for the specification and analysis of behavioral structures such as value functions, invariants, and bisimulation relations through local, one-step system dynamics. It provides soundness guarantees for transferring behavioral structures between abstract and concrete systems and enables the construction of quantitative metrics from logical behavioral semantics. The framework addresses the lack of a general principle for determining which behavioral structures are preserved under state abstraction. By offering reusable definitions and proof principles, it establishes a principled foundation for reasoning about behaviors in reinforcement learning, facilitating scalability and robustness in learning algorithms applied to structured environments.

items.title: Researchers introduce FactorLibrary to find minimal arithmetic circuits for polynomials using reinforcement learning with 91.8% success on circuits up to complexity 8 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed FactorLibrary, a new approach that uses reinforcement learning to find minimal arithmetic circuits for polynomials over finite fields, a complex problem in algebraic complexity theory. By framing the task as a reinforcement learning challenge from both bottom-up and top-down perspectives, they introduced FactorLibrary to store reusable subexpressions as subgoals, helping to manage the rapidly expanding search space. Their top-down agent using PPO combined with Monte Carlo Tree Search achieved a 91.8% success rate in identifying certified optimal circuits up to complexity 8. The study involved training multiple agents with different reinforcement learning algorithms, including Gumbel-PPO-MCTS for the bottom-up approach and PPO+MCTS and SAC for the top-down methods. Among these, the PPO+MCTS top-down agent demonstrated the most consistent and stable performance, effectively navigating the combinatorial complexity inherent in the problem. This advancement offers a promising direction for automating the discovery of efficient arithmetic circuits, which are fundamental in computational mathematics and theoretical computer science.

items.title: Researchers show data curation inducing brevity in vision-language models improves inference efficiency by 35x in FLOPs per correct answer with minimal accuracy loss [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated that curating training data to encourage brevity in vision-language models (VLMs) significantly improves inference efficiency, achieving up to a 35-fold reduction in computational cost per correct answer with minimal loss in accuracy. By training models on concise and accurate data, the study shows that these models produce shorter outputs, lowering the overall cost of inference without sacrificing performance. The team applied their data curation approach to the MAmmoTH-VL dataset and evaluated multiple VLMs ranging from 1 billion to 4 billion parameters. Their results indicate that models trained on curated data outperform those trained on standard datasets and other open-weight models, gaining both efficiency and accuracy. Notably, the concise models reached correct answers missed by more verbose reasoning models, suggesting that brevity targets inference efficiency directly without compromising reasoning quality. This work highlights brevity as a crucial, previously underexplored factor in improving inference efficiency, complementing existing methods like pruning and quantization. It suggests that focusing on output length through data curation can be a practical and effective strategy to reduce computational demands in large-scale vision-language models.

items.title: Researchers propose CPTabKAN, a concept-guided polynomial tabular Kolmogorov-Arnold network for interpretable EEG-based mild cognitive impairment detection, achieving 0.9038 weighted F1-score on 372-subject cohort [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed CPTabKAN, a novel interpretable machine learning framework for detecting mild cognitive impairment (MCI) using EEG data. This approach integrates physiologically informed concept encoding, polynomial feature expansion to capture interactions, and a nonlinear tabular classifier, achieving a weighted F1-score of 0.9038 on a cohort of 372 subjects. CPTabKAN outperformed traditional methods like GradientBoosting, demonstrating improved accuracy and interpretability in MCI detection from sleep EEG recordings. The model organizes 1,379 EEG-derived features into ten physiologically motivated concept groups and uses a degree-2 polynomial transformation to reveal first- and second-order interactions among features. Evaluation on the Study of Osteoporotic Fractures cohort showed that CPTabKAN's components each contribute independently to performance, with key features including power spectral density, multi-scale entropy, and Hjorth parameters. Cross-concept interactions involving complexity measures, statistics, demographics, and slow oscillations were particularly influential. These findings suggest that concept-structured, interaction-aware tabular learning can provide physiologically coherent reasoning, enhancing clinical trust in EEG-based MCI screening. The approach offers a scalable and interpretable alternative to existing EEG analysis methods, potentially aiding early diagnosis and intervention for cognitive decline.

items.title: Researchers propose TopoCast, a topology-driven framework to evaluate structural fidelity in Transformer-based time series forecasting, revealing errors overlooked by conventional metrics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced TopoCast, a novel topology-driven framework designed to evaluate the structural fidelity of Transformer-based time series forecasting models. Unlike traditional evaluation methods that rely on pointwise error metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), TopoCast assesses intrinsic dynamic properties of forecast signals, including recurrent patterns, oscillations, and phase alignment, which are often missed by conventional metrics. TopoCast reconstructs phase-space representations of forecast and actual sequences using Takens delay embedding and applies persistent homology to capture their underlying dynamics. The framework derives multiple topological fidelity measures aggregated into a Topological Fidelity Score (TFS) and introduces a dominant cycle overlap metric to evaluate the timing of oscillatory patterns. Together, these yield the Localized Topological Fidelity Score (LTFS), which detects temporal localization errors invisible to existing evaluation approaches. Experiments on five Transformer architectures across three benchmark datasets reveal that models with similar numerical errors can differ significantly in structural fidelity, highlighting the importance of topology-aware evaluation in time series forecasting.

items.title: Researchers propose single-rollout proximal policy optimization using Monte Carlo Pass@k critic for token-level credit assignment in language model reinforcement learning, showing gains on mathematical reasoning benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced a single-rollout proximal policy optimization (SR-PPO) method that improves token-level credit assignment in reinforcement learning for language models. This approach uses a Monte Carlo Pass@k critic to estimate the success probability of prompt prefixes from a single rollout, addressing challenges in scaling episodic experience collection and sparse reward attribution. The method prioritizes difficult prefixes and provides a more selective learning signal than traditional Pass@1 metrics. SR-PPO avoids the computational expense of repeated sampling by training a calibrated token-level credit critic that predicts Pass@k success probabilities, which converge to a reachability indicator as k increases. This enables efficient credit assignment without sampling multiple contrasting traces. Initial experiments demonstrate stable learning and consistent improvements in Pass@128 success rates on mathematical reasoning benchmarks such as HMMT26 and AIME24, highlighting the potential of this technique for enhancing language model reinforcement learning.

items.title: Researchers propose boundary-based policy approximations for structured Markov decision processes, showing lower error and faster convergence than reinforcement learning in inventory and queue control experiments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced a boundary-based approach to policy approximation in structured Markov decision processes, focusing on learning policy regions directly rather than approximating high-dimensional value functions. Their method leverages the simpler geometry of optimal policies, resulting in lower policy errors, smaller value gaps, and faster convergence compared to traditional reinforcement learning techniques. Experiments in inventory control and queue admission demonstrate the approach's improved stability and efficiency. The study also presents a policy-loss decomposition that connects performance degradation to action margins, explaining why errors tend to cluster near decision boundaries where actions are indifferent. This insight helps clarify the advantages of boundary-based approximations over value function approximations in these settings.

items.title: Researchers present Expresso-AI, a video-based deep learning framework with explainable facial analysis for automatic depression severity diagnosis, improving interpretability and predictive performance on AVEC dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Expresso-AI, a video-based deep learning framework designed to diagnose depression severity automatically through explainable facial analysis. By fine-tuning deep convolutional neural networks pre-trained on action recognition datasets with facial videos from the AVEC depression dataset, the framework provides both visual and quantitative explanations of its decisions, enhancing interpretability for healthcare professionals. This approach not only improves the understanding of the model's reasoning by analyzing facial regions and temporal expression semantics but also achieves better predictive performance compared to previous single-face benchmarks. The framework addresses a critical gap in automated depression diagnosis by focusing on affect-specificity and interpretability, which are essential for practical application in mental health care. By generating saliency maps and temporal activity insights, Expresso-AI offers a multidisciplinary tool that supports early diagnosis and intervention, facilitating effective collaboration and treatment planning in mental health services.

items.title: Researchers present TL++, a traversal-learning framework that improves accuracy and privacy in distributed intelligent systems by reducing communication and enabling activation-level secret sharing [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed TL++, a traversal-learning framework designed to enhance accuracy and privacy in distributed intelligent systems by enabling training across data silos without centralizing raw data. TL++ operates in two modes: a base mode that exchanges cut-layer activations and gradients instead of full models, and a secure mode that secret-shares these activations and gradients between servers to prevent exposure of plaintext data. This approach aims to recover centralized mini-batch gradient behavior while reducing communication overhead and protecting sensitive information in a semi-honest two-server setting. The framework was evaluated against federated and split-learning baselines on datasets including CIFAR-10 and BioGPT/PubMedQA, demonstrating significant improvements. On CIFAR-10, TL++ achieved accuracies exceeding the best non-TL++ baselines by over 12 percentage points and reduced per-step communication by more than 13 times compared to full-model synchronization. These results suggest that TL++ approaches the performance of centralized training while offering enhanced privacy and communication efficiency.

items.title: Researchers present gradient-based inverse lithography for EUV masks using differentiable waveguide method and physics-informed neural operator, demonstrating mask design achieving desired wafer fields at 11.2 nm wavelength [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a gradient-based inverse lithography technology for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) masks, utilizing a differentiable waveguide method and a physics-informed neural operator called the waveguide neural operator (WGNO). This approach treats these methods as end-to-end physics engines, enabling the recovery of the absorber's permittivity on the mask through automatic differentiation of the full forward diffraction model. Numerical experiments with realistic 2D and 3D mask absorbers at an 11.2 nm wavelength demonstrate that this method can design mask structures that achieve the desired field patterns on the wafer. The study focuses on materials such as TaBN, La, and U for the mask absorbers and validates the effectiveness of the inverse lithography techniques in producing precise mask designs. By integrating physics-based modeling with neural operators, the framework offers a novel and efficient way to optimize EUV mask patterns, which are critical for advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes.

items.title: OncoSynth introduces a diffusion-based machine learning framework for synthetic oncology data generation, improving treatment effect estimation accuracy by up to 66% on lung and breast cancer cohorts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OncoSynth is a new machine learning framework that generates synthetic oncology data to improve the accuracy of treatment effect estimation. It uses a diffusion-based sequential approach to model the causal relationships between patient covariates, treatment assignments, and survival outcomes. Evaluated on large lung and breast cancer cohorts, OncoSynth produces synthetic patient data that closely mirrors real-world distributions and reduces errors in treatment effect estimation by up to 66% at the population level and 58% at the patient level compared to existing methods. This framework addresses the challenge of restricted access to patient-level data in oncology by enabling reliable analysis of treatment effectiveness through synthetic cohorts. By preserving causal relationships in the data, OncoSynth supports more precise evidence generation for personalized cancer treatment, particularly in settings where data sharing is limited.

items.title: Researchers propose MiniOpt, a reinforcement learning framework that models and solves general optimization problems with limited training resources, achieving strong generalization across diverse tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced MiniOpt, a reinforcement learning framework designed to solve a wide range of optimization problems efficiently with limited training resources. MiniOpt employs a "reasoning-to-model-and-solve" approach that breaks down optimization tasks into structured modeling and solver generation, supported by a novel reward function called OptReward that evaluates both problem formulation and solution quality without needing expert demonstrations. This framework enhances exploration and stabilizes learning for compact models, achieving strong generalization across diverse optimization types and scenarios. Extensive testing shows that MiniOpt-3B outperforms other models with fewer than 10 billion parameters in solving accuracy, while remaining competitive among larger models. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining optimization-oriented reward design with reinforcement learning to develop compact language models specialized in optimization tasks. The code for MiniOpt is publicly available for further research and development.

items.title: Researchers propose Semantic Consistency Policy Optimization to improve reinforcement learning for LLM agents, achieving over 93% success on ALFWorld and 74% on WebShop with 1.5B parameters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Semantic Consistency Policy Optimization (SCPO), a new method to improve reinforcement learning for large language model (LLM) agents tackling long-horizon, sparse-reward tasks. SCPO addresses the issue of inconsistent credit assignment in group-based reinforcement learning by assigning positive step-level credit to failed steps based on their similarity to successful steps within the same rollout group. This approach enhances learning by recovering partially correct progress from failed attempts. Testing SCPO on the ALFWorld and WebShop benchmarks, the method achieved success rates of over 93% and 74%, respectively, using models with 1.5 billion parameters. The improvements were especially notable on the most challenging multi-step tasks, demonstrating SCPO's effectiveness in refining policy optimization for complex LLM agent behaviors.

items.title: Researchers find trigger color significantly affects success of semantic backdoor attacks in federated learning, with white and black triggers targeting different classes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that the color of visual triggers significantly influences the success of semantic backdoor attacks in federated learning. By using natural accessories like masks and sunglasses in black and white variants as triggers, attackers can poison updates to misclassify images while maintaining normal task performance. Experiments on a hair-color classification task showed that white triggers are more effective for targeting the blond class, while black triggers work better for the black class, even when other factors remain constant. The study analyzed these attacks under both standard poisoning objectives and a more advanced approach that balances attack effectiveness with minimizing detection by keeping malicious updates close to the global model. The findings persisted even under robust aggregation methods, highlighting that trigger color is a critical factor in the design and evaluation of semantic backdoor mechanisms in federated learning systems.

items.title: Researchers find medical records and cardiac biomarkers outperform vascular graph neural networks for pulmonary embolism risk stratification using CTPA data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers investigated the effectiveness of using medical records, cardiac biomarkers, and vascular graph neural networks (GNNs) derived from computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) data to stratify risk in patients with pulmonary embolism (PE). Their study, based on a dataset of 353 patients with comprehensive data, found that medical records and cardiac biomarkers were the most significant predictors for PE risk, while vascular biomarkers and GNNs applied to vascular graphs did not improve risk stratification beyond traditional tabular models. The study benchmarked various approaches combining these data sources and explored why vascular graph-based models underperformed. The findings suggest that, contrary to expectations, vascular graph representations may not contain discriminative information useful for PE risk stratification. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration.

items.title: Researchers present MAGR-BB, a multi-agent goal recognition method using team- and goal-conditioned reinforcement learning with factorized branch-and-bound search, reducing hypothesis evaluation and runtime on Blocksworld benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MAGR-BB, a multi-agent goal recognition method that uses team- and goal-conditioned reinforcement learning combined with a factorized branch-and-bound search to efficiently infer which agents are working together and their objectives. This approach addresses the challenge of a rapidly growing hypothesis space in multi-agent scenarios by ranking team-goal hypotheses based solely on observed agent trajectories. MAGR-BB matches the accuracy of exhaustive search on a multi-agent Blocksworld benchmark while significantly reducing the number of hypotheses evaluated and the overall recognition runtime. The method employs a shared policy conditioned on both team composition and goals as a scoring model within the branch-and-bound framework, enabling efficient pruning of unlikely hypotheses. This advancement is particularly relevant for applications like drone surveillance and collaborative robotics, where only agent trajectories are observable and timely goal recognition is critical.

items.title: Researchers present HiReLC, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for automated joint pruning and quantization of neural networks achieving up to 6.72× compression with minimal accuracy loss [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed HiReLC, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework designed to automate the joint pruning and quantization of deep neural networks. This approach uses low-level agents to optimize configurations per network block and high-level agents to allocate global compression budgets, guided by sensitivity estimates. HiReLC achieves compression ratios up to 6.72 times with minimal accuracy loss, demonstrating its effectiveness across Vision Transformer and CNN benchmarks. The framework incorporates an iterative active learning loop that combines surrogate-guided reinforcement learning with fine-tuning to reduce computational costs. Its architecture-agnostic design allows it to adapt to various network topologies, making it a versatile tool for neural network compression. Experimental results show compression ratios between 5.99 and 6.72 times, with accuracy changes ranging from a 3.83% gain to a 5.62% drop, highlighting the practical benefits of hierarchical policy decomposition and sensitivity-aware guidance in model compression.

items.title: Researchers propose a baseline protocol for model forensics to determine if concerning AI behavior reflects misalignment or benign causes, tested on six agentic environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced a baseline protocol for model forensics aimed at determining whether concerning AI behavior stems from misalignment or benign causes. The protocol involves analyzing the model's chain of thought to generate hypotheses about its behavior, followed by testing these hypotheses through modifications to prompts or environments. This approach was evaluated across six agentic environments where models exhibited concerning actions. The study demonstrated that certain behaviors, such as shortcuts taken by the Kimi K2 Thinking model, were due to a genuine preference for low-effort actions, while DeepSeek R1's deceptive behavior was linked to a desire for self-consistency. Although the protocol provides valuable insights, the researchers acknowledge limitations, including challenges in confirming some beliefs without positive controls. Overall, this work establishes a foundational step in the emerging field of model forensics, offering a framework for future improvements.

items.title: Researchers show reinforcement learning post-training provides effective step-level scoring for LLM agents without dedicated reward models, validated across five benchmarks and four model families [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated that reinforcement learning (RL) post-training can effectively provide step-level scoring for large language model (LLM) agents without the need for dedicated reward models. They introduced the concept of "progress advantage," an implicit advantage derived from the log-probability ratio between the RL-trained policy and its reference policy, which accurately recovers the optimal advantage function. This approach is annotation-free, domain-agnostic, and integrates seamlessly into the standard RL post-training process. The team validated the progress advantage across five benchmarks and four model families, applying it to test-time scaling, uncertainty quantification, and failure attribution. Their results show that this method consistently outperforms confidence-based baselines and even surpasses specialized trained reward models, despite requiring no task-specific training. Additional analyses provide practical guidance for implementing this technique in real-world agentic systems.

items.title: Researchers find on-policy self-distillation with sampled demonstrations reduces output diversity and flattens pass@k accuracy curves despite matching reinforcement learning performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that on-policy self-distillation, which uses a single model as both teacher and student conditioned on correct demonstrations, achieves strong pass@1 accuracy but reduces output diversity and flattens pass@k accuracy curves. This means that generating more rollouts does not improve accuracy, as the method channels feedback through the model's own biases, amplifying existing probability gaps and concentrating on dominant outputs. While self-distilled models match or exceed reinforcement learning (RL) in average performance on tasks like graph path-finding and science question answering, they show substantially lower functional and semantic diversity and struggle with out-of-distribution scenarios requiring diverse strategies. The study theoretically analyzes the optimal self-distillation policy, revealing that it tilts the base distribution based on conditional mutual information between student rollouts and the correct rollout used as context. Unlike ideal on-policy RL, which maintains probability ratios among equally correct rollouts, self-distillation can intensify biases, leading to less varied outputs. These findings highlight a trade-off between accuracy and diversity in self-distillation approaches, with implications for their robustness and generalization in complex tasks.

items.title: Researchers develop LLM-Verifier Convergence Theorem proving termination and a 4/δ latency bound for multi-stage formal verification pipelines, validated by over 90,000 trials [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed the LLM-Verifier Convergence Theorem, a formal framework that guarantees termination and provides a latency bound for multi-stage formal verification pipelines integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with formal verification tools. By modeling the verification process as a sequential absorbing Markov Chain with four key stages-CodeGen, Compilation, InvariantSynth, and SMTSolving-they proved that the system almost surely reaches a verified state for any non-zero stage success probability, with an expected latency bounded by 4 divided by this probability. This theoretical result was validated through over 90,000 empirical trials, all of which successfully reached verification and showed convergence factors closely matching the predicted bound. The study also identified three operational zones-marginal, practical, and high-performance-and proposed a dynamic calibration strategy to manage parameter drift in real-world applications. These contributions establish a rigorous foundation for predictable resource planning and performance management in safety-critical software verification systems.

items.title: Researchers present FlexMS, a unified public benchmark framework standardizing molecule tandem mass spectrum prediction with difficulty-aware diagnostics and modular evaluation protocols [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced FlexMS, a unified public benchmark framework designed to standardize the prediction of molecule tandem mass spectra (MS/MS). FlexMS addresses challenges in evaluating and deploying deep learning models for spectrum prediction by integrating molecular encoders, metadata conditioning, predictor heads, and downstream retrieval into a single protocol. This framework enables fair comparisons across models and datasets, overcoming inconsistencies and limitations found in current approaches. FlexMS incorporates difficulty-aware diagnostics alongside aggregate accuracy metrics, offering detailed insights into model performance under varying computational resources, data scales, and retrieval tasks. By providing a modular and reproducible evaluation environment, FlexMS aims to facilitate the development and selection of robust predictive tools in metabolomics, helping the community identify stable algorithmic conclusions and practical operating points.

items.title: Researchers present a non-vacuous generalization bound for deep neural networks using stochastic gradient optimization and fractal hypothesis sets, validated on ResNet and Vision Transformer with ImageNet-1K [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a new theoretical generalization bound for deep neural networks that is both simple and non-vacuous, addressing a key challenge in understanding how well these models perform on unseen data. Their approach leverages the fractal-like nature of the hypothesis sets accessed by stochastic gradient algorithms, enabling a tighter bound based on algorithm-dependent Rademacher complexity. This method models the discrete-time recursion of training as a continuous-time stochastic differential equation driven by fractional Brownian motion. The researchers validated their approach through numerical studies on modern neural network architectures such as ResNet and Vision Transformer, demonstrating plausible generalization guarantees even when trained on large-scale datasets like ImageNet-1K. This work offers a promising optimization perspective for deriving meaningful generalization bounds beyond existing loose or compression-based methods.

items.title: Researchers propose Parameter Vulnerability Factor (PVF) metric to quantify AI model susceptibility to silent data corruptions, analyzing DLRM, CNN, and BERT models during inference [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced the Parameter Vulnerability Factor (PVF), a new metric designed to quantify the susceptibility of AI models to silent data corruptions (SDCs) that can alter model parameters during inference. PVF measures the likelihood that a corruption in a specific parameter will cause an incorrect output, providing a standardized way to assess AI model reliability. The study applies PVF to three AI tasks-recommendation systems (DLRM), vision classification (CNN), and text classification (BERT)-with a detailed vulnerability analysis focused on DLRM. This metric addresses growing concerns about the reliability of AI systems amid increasing hardware complexity and faults. PVF draws inspiration from the architectural vulnerability factor used in computer architecture and has been instrumental in guiding error management decisions in the deployment of Meta's in-house AI chip, MTIA. By identifying how different model components vary in vulnerability, PVF offers valuable insights for improving AI system robustness against parameter corruptions.

items.title: Researchers propose ACT-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture combining imitation and self-supervised learning to improve policy representation and world model accuracy by up to 40% [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced ACT-JEPA, a novel architecture that combines imitation learning (IL) and self-supervised learning (SSL) to improve policy representation and world model accuracy. This approach jointly predicts action sequences and latent observation sequences, enabling the model to learn in latent space and filter out irrelevant details. Evaluations across various environments and tasks show that ACT-JEPA outperforms existing methods, achieving up to a 40% improvement in world model understanding and a 10% increase in task success rate. ACT-JEPA addresses limitations of traditional IL, which relies on costly expert demonstrations and lacks explicit environmental understanding, by integrating SSL to learn from diverse, unlabeled data. The use of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture allows efficient learning in latent space, enhancing the robustness of the world model. The study demonstrates that predicting latent observation sequences generalizes well to predicting action sequences, highlighting the benefits of combining IL and SSL for efficient policy learning and improved decision-making performance.

items.title: Researchers propose high-order reciprocal-based control barrier functions for safe reinforcement learning control with performance and stability guarantees in nonlinear systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a new approach to reinforcement learning-based control for nonlinear systems that ensures both safety and performance. They introduce high-order reciprocal-based control barrier functions to manage complex state constraints and unknown disturbances without requiring disturbance bounds. This method integrates gradient similarity concepts and adaptive mechanisms within a model-based safe reinforcement learning framework to enhance system performance while maintaining safety guarantees. The proposed approach addresses the challenge of balancing safety and optimality in learning control by extending control barrier function designs to handle high-relative-degree constraints robustly. Simulation examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithms in maintaining safety and improving performance despite unknown time-varying disturbances and actuator faults.

items.title: Researchers introduce OmegAMP, a diffusion-based model for targeted antimicrobial peptide generation with 96% experimental success against multi-drug resistant strains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed OmegAMP, a diffusion-based deep learning framework designed to generate antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) with high precision and controllability. This model incorporates a novel conditioning mechanism and biologically informed encoding to target specific physicochemical properties and activity profiles, including species-specific effectiveness. In laboratory tests, 24 out of 25 candidate peptides generated by OmegAMP demonstrated antimicrobial activity, including effectiveness against multi-drug resistant strains, achieving a 96% success rate. OmegAMP also employs a synthetic data augmentation strategy to train classifiers that filter AMPs, significantly reducing false positives and improving experimental outcomes. The framework shows state-of-the-art performance in computational AMP discovery, addressing key challenges such as limited controllability and low hit rates in previous deep learning approaches. These results highlight OmegAMP's potential to advance computational methods in combating antimicrobial resistance, offering a promising tool for developing new treatments against resistant pathogens.

items.title: Researchers propose FiMi-RM framework to model and mitigate length bias in reward models for RLHF, improving alignment and reducing verbosity in language model outputs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced FiMi-RM, a new framework designed to address length bias in reward models used in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). Length bias occurs when reward models favor longer responses regardless of their quality, leading to reward hacking where models optimize for length rather than genuine alignment with human preferences. FiMi-RM autonomously learns and corrects these biases by modeling the non-linear relationship between response length and reward, thereby improving the alignment of language models with human preferences while reducing verbosity. The FiMi-RM approach involves three stages: training a standard reward model that contains length bias, fitting a lightweight model to capture the complex length-reward relationship, and integrating this correction into the reward model to decouple length from reward without losing preference modeling capabilities. Experimental results show that FiMi-RM achieves a more balanced length-reward distribution and enhances performance when applied to alignment algorithms like Direct Preference Optimization and Best-of-N, improving length-controlled win rates and reducing unnecessary verbosity.

items.title: Researchers show sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) improves deep neural network calibration and propose CSAM variant with lower calibration error on ImageNet-1K and other datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated that sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), a training technique for deep neural networks, improves model calibration by reducing overconfidence in predictions. Their theoretical analysis indicates that SAM enhances calibration by implicitly maximizing the entropy of the predictive distribution, leading to better-calibrated models compared to standard training methods like stochastic gradient descent. To further improve calibration, the team proposed a variant called CSAM, which consistently achieves lower calibration errors than SAM and other approaches across multiple datasets, including ImageNet-1K. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of SAM and CSAM in safety-critical applications where reliable confidence estimates are crucial, such as medical diagnosis and autonomous driving. The findings suggest that these methods can mitigate the risks associated with poorly calibrated neural networks, potentially enhancing the trustworthiness of AI systems in real-world scenarios.

items.title: Researchers propose HiT-JEPA, a hierarchical self-supervised framework for multi-scale urban trajectory embedding and similarity computation, validated on multiple real-world datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced HiT-JEPA, a hierarchical self-supervised framework designed to improve the representation of urban trajectory data by capturing multi-scale spatial movement patterns. This approach addresses limitations in existing models by integrating fine-grained details, intermediate patterns, and high-level abstractions within a unified three-layer hierarchy, enabling a comprehensive understanding of both local dynamics and global semantics. The framework was validated through extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in trajectory similarity computation. HiT-JEPA's design allows it to capture diverse and complementary information across different semantic levels, resulting in richer trajectory representations. The researchers have made the code publicly available to support further exploration and application of their method.

items.title: Researchers introduce BALD-GFlowNet, a generative active learning method using GFlowNets to scale virtual drug screening independent of unlabeled pool size, matching BALD performance with more diverse molecules [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed BALD-GFlowNet, a generative active learning method that uses Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) to efficiently sample molecules for virtual drug screening. This approach addresses the scalability limitations of traditional pool-based active learning methods like Bayesian Active Learning by Disagreement (BALD), which struggle with the computational cost of evaluating extremely large unlabeled datasets. BALD-GFlowNet achieves performance comparable to BALD while generating a more diverse set of molecules, independent of the size of the unlabeled pool. By replacing the conventional pool-based acquisition process with generative sampling proportional to the BALD reward, BALD-GFlowNet enables scalable and efficient exploration of vast chemical libraries. This advancement offers a promising direction for accelerating molecular discovery in drug development by balancing informativeness and diversity in sample selection.

items.title: Researchers propose Conjecturing-Proving Loop using LLMs for iterative theorem discovery and proof verification in Lean 4, improving proof success via in-context learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a new pipeline called the Conjecturing-Proving Loop (CPL) that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to iteratively generate and prove mathematical conjectures in Lean 4. This approach improves proof success by conditioning each iteration on previously verified theorems and proofs, enabling the model to refine its strategies through in-context learning without additional parameters. The study provides both theoretical and experimental evidence that CPL enhances the discovery of challenging theorems compared to methods that generate statements and proofs simultaneously. The key innovation of CPL lies in its reuse of the LLM's own formally verified outputs as context for subsequent proof attempts, which consistently boosts proof success rates. This self-generated in-context learning demonstrates a promising direction for neural theorem proving, and the researchers have made their source code publicly available to support further exploration and development in this area.

items.title: Researchers propose Distribution Preference Optimization (DiPO) for LLM unlearning, targeting next-token distributions to improve forget quality and utility preservation on TOFU and MUSE benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Distribution Preference Optimization (DiPO), a novel method for unlearning in large language models (LLMs) that targets next-token probability distributions to improve the removal of specific data influences while preserving overall model utility. DiPO addresses limitations of previous optimization-based unlearning methods by focusing on distribution-level preferences, constructed through selective amplification or suppression of high-confidence output logits. This approach enhances forget quality and utility preservation without requiring domain-specific knowledge or complex prompts. The team theoretically validated DiPO's loss function alignment with desired unlearning goals and conducted extensive experiments demonstrating its effectiveness. DiPO achieved the highest forget quality on the TOFU benchmark and showed superior scalability and sustainability in utility preservation on the MUSE benchmark, indicating a strong balance between forgetting targeted data and maintaining model performance.

items.title: Researchers propose weight space representation learning using neural field adaptation with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to improve 2D and 3D data tasks and latent diffusion model generation quality [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have explored the use of neural network weights as effective representations by applying low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to constrain the optimization space within a pre-trained base model. This approach, focusing on neural fields, demonstrates that multiplicative LoRA weights can capture high-quality, distinctive, and semantically structured representations across various tasks involving 2D and 3D data. The study shows that when these multiplicative LoRA weights are integrated with latent diffusion models, they enable higher-quality data generation compared to existing weight-space methods. This advancement suggests a promising direction for improving reconstruction, generation, and analysis tasks in machine learning applications involving complex data types.

items.title: Researchers introduce auto-exploration methods for online reinforcement learning that automatically explore state and action spaces with parameter-free algorithms achieving O(ε⁻²) sample complexity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed new auto-exploration methods for online reinforcement learning that automatically explore both state and action spaces without relying on algorithm-dependent parameters. These parameter-free algorithms achieve a sample complexity of O(ε⁻²) to reach an ε error, improving upon existing approaches that require assumptions of sufficient exploration and often yield suboptimal or non-implementable solutions. The methods apply to both tabular and linear function approximation settings and integrate auto-exploration into policy mirror descent to avoid dependence on unknown stationary distributions. In the tabular setting, the approach introduces a dynamic exploration time with a data-driven stopping criterion, while for linear function approximation, it proposes a new sampling distribution based on discounted visitation that covers a broader class of Markov chains. These innovations simplify implementation and provide theoretical guarantees under assumptions about the existence of an exploring optimal policy, marking a significant advancement in efficient reinforcement learning algorithms.

items.title: Researchers introduce STGAT framework to detect clock drift and Y2K38 timestamp failures in energy IoT systems, achieving 95.7% accuracy and reducing detection delay by 26% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed STGAT, a Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network framework designed to detect clock drift and Year 2038 (Y2K38) timestamp failures in energy Internet of Things (IoT) systems. This framework addresses vulnerabilities in time integrity that affect distributed IoT devices in energy cyber-physical systems like smart grids and microgrids, achieving 95.7% accuracy in identifying temporal anomalies and reducing detection delay by 26%. STGAT models both temporal distortions and spatial propagation of timing errors, improving upon traditional anomaly detection methods that assume reliable timestamps. STGAT integrates drift-aware temporal embeddings and temporal self-attention to capture corrupted time evolution at individual devices, while graph attention mechanisms model inter-device timing error propagation. A curvature-regularized latent representation helps distinguish normal clock behavior from anomalies caused by drift, synchronization offsets, and overflow events. Experimental evaluations on energy IoT telemetry with controlled timing perturbations demonstrated that STGAT outperforms recurrent, transformer, and other graph-based models, maintaining stable performance under various timing inconsistencies.

items.title: Researchers introduce Clifford Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (ClKAN) for function approximation in Clifford Algebra spaces using Randomized Quasi-Monte Carlo grids and new batch normalization methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed the Clifford Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (ClKAN), a novel architecture designed for efficient function approximation within Clifford Algebra spaces. To address the challenge of exponential scaling in higher-dimensional algebras, the team employs Randomized Quasi-Monte Carlo grid generation. Additionally, ClKAN incorporates new batch normalization techniques to manage variable domain inputs effectively. The ClKAN model has been validated through synthetic and physics-inspired tasks, demonstrating its potential applications in scientific discovery and engineering. This approach offers a flexible and scalable solution for complex function approximation problems in advanced mathematical spaces.

items.title: Researchers present CauScale, a neural architecture for efficient causal discovery scaling inference to graphs with up to 1000 nodes and delivering up to 13,000 times faster inference [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed CauScale, a neural architecture designed to efficiently perform causal discovery on large graphs with up to 1000 nodes. CauScale addresses significant time and space efficiency challenges faced by existing methods by compressing data embeddings and using tied attention weights, enabling it to scale where previous approaches could not. The model maintains high accuracy through a two-stream design that extracts relational evidence and integrates statistical graph priors. During training, CauScale successfully handled graphs with 500 nodes, surpassing prior methods limited by space constraints. It achieved 99.6% mean average precision on in-distribution data and 84.4% on out-of-distribution data, while providing inference speed improvements ranging from 4 to 13,000 times compared to earlier techniques. This advancement has potential implications for scientific AI and data analysis fields requiring scalable causal discovery.

items.title: Researchers show neural networks with trainable low-degree rational activation functions are more expressive and parameter-efficient than standard activations, with exponential approximation advantages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated that neural networks using trainable low-degree rational activation functions are more expressive and parameter-efficient than those employing common fixed activations like ReLU, Sigmoid, and Tanh. Their study shows that rational-activation networks can approximate functions with exponentially fewer parameters compared to networks with standard activations, establishing a significant theoretical advantage in approximation capabilities. The team proved that for a given error tolerance, rational networks require only a polylogarithmic increase in size to approximate any network with fixed activations, while the reverse demands a logarithmic parameter increase. This exponential efficiency extends to complex architectures, including gated activations and transformer-style nonlinearities. Moreover, rational activations integrate smoothly into existing training frameworks, often matching or surpassing the performance of fixed activations under identical conditions.

items.title: Researchers propose a hybrid TGN-SEAL model that improves dynamic graph link prediction by integrating local topology and temporal information, boosting average precision by at least 2% on sparse datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a hybrid model combining Temporal Graph Networks (TGN) with a subgraph extraction technique called SEAL to improve link prediction in sparse, dynamic networks. This approach integrates local structural information with temporal dynamics, addressing limitations of existing methods that struggle with data sparsity and temporal dependencies. The model demonstrated at least a 2% increase in average precision over standard TGNs on datasets including telecommunication call records, emails, and messages. The study highlights that conventional graph neural networks and snapshot-based methods often fail to capture evolving interactions effectively, especially in networks with transient links. By extracting enclosing subgraphs around candidate links, the hybrid model jointly learns both the network's local topology and its temporal evolution, enhancing predictive accuracy in challenging sparse conditions. This advancement suggests that incorporating local structural context into temporal graph models can lead to more robust link prediction in continuously evolving networks. The improved performance on real-world sparse datasets indicates potential applications in telecommunications and communication networks where dynamic interactions are common.

items.title: Researchers show logit distance bounds linear representational similarity in discriminative models, improving distillation over KL divergence methods in synthetic and image datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have demonstrated that for a broad class of discriminative models, including autoregressive language models, closeness in a logit-based distance measure guarantees linear representational similarity between models. This finding contrasts with previous observations that closeness in KL divergence does not necessarily imply such similarity. The study defines a representational dissimilarity measure bounded by the logit distance and shows that while KL divergence can upper-bound logit distance, it often fails to provide meaningful control in practice. The research highlights that KL-based distillation methods may replicate a teacher model's predictions without preserving important linear representational properties, such as the recoverability of human-interpretable concepts. Experiments on synthetic and image datasets reveal that distillation using logit-distance leads to student models with higher linear representational similarity and better retention of the teacher's linearly recoverable features, suggesting improved distillation performance over traditional KL divergence approaches.

items.title: Researchers develop eight surrogate neural network models for rock-fluid interaction in porous media, introducing a grid-size-invariant approach that reduces memory use and outperforms reduced-order models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed eight surrogate neural network models to predict fluid flow in porous media, addressing the computational challenges of traditional high-fidelity numerical models used for rock-fluid interaction. These models include four reduced-order models (ROMs) and four grid-size-invariant neural networks, which can infer results on larger computational domains than those used during training. The study finds that the grid-size-invariant approach reduces memory consumption during training and outperforms the ROMs in predictive accuracy. The research compares UNet and UNet++ architectures, demonstrating that UNet++ provides better performance for surrogate modeling. The application focuses on fluid-induced rock dissolution, a complex scenario due to the dynamic nature of the solid field, which complicates future predictions. This work offers a more efficient alternative for multi-query problems like uncertainty quantification and optimization, where numerous simulations are required.

items.title: Researchers introduce MONET, a multi-task optimization algorithm modeling task spaces as graphs to improve knowledge transfer and scalability across thousands of tasks, outperforming MAP-Elites baselines in four domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MONET (Multi-Task Optimization over Networks of Tasks), a novel algorithm designed to improve multi-task optimization by modeling the task space as a graph where tasks are nodes connected by edges. This approach facilitates knowledge transfer between tasks and efficiently handles high-dimensional problems by leveraging the topology of the task space. MONET integrates social learning, which generates new candidates through crossover among neighboring tasks, with individual learning that refines solutions via mutation. The algorithm was tested across four domains-archery, arm, cartpole with 5,000 tasks each, and hexapod with 2,000 tasks-and demonstrated performance that matches or surpasses existing MAP-Elites-based methods. MONET addresses scalability issues faced by population-based methods and improves upon previous approaches that rely on fixed, discretized archives, making it a promising advancement for large-scale multi-task optimization.

items.title: Researchers introduce SplitZip, a GPU-optimized lossless KV cache compressor for disaggregated LLM serving achieving over 600 GB/s compression and 1.3× transfer speedup [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed SplitZip, a GPU-optimized lossless compression method designed to accelerate the transfer of key-value (KV) caches in disaggregated large language model (LLM) serving systems. SplitZip efficiently compresses KV tensors by exploiting redundancies in floating-point exponents, achieving compression and decompression speeds exceeding 600 GB/s and 2,100 GB/s respectively, which significantly outperforms existing lossless codecs. This advancement addresses the bottleneck caused by transferring KV caches between prefill and decode workers located on separate physical systems, particularly benefiting long-input and agentic workloads. SplitZip integrates seamlessly into current serving frameworks without altering model execution and uses a fixed-length coding scheme for frequent exponent values alongside a sparse escape stream for rare exponents. Experiments demonstrate up to a 1.32× speedup in KV cache transfer and notable improvements in throughput metrics. The approach also extends to FP8 KV caches, offering additional compression gains. The code for SplitZip is publicly available for further research and application.

items.title: Researchers propose inertial tracking framework using bicycle mechanical constraints and mixture-of-experts model to improve shared bike localization accuracy by 12% in GNSS-blocked urban environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed an inertial tracking framework that combines bicycle mechanical constraints with a mixture-of-experts model to enhance the localization accuracy of shared bikes in urban environments where GNSS signals are blocked. This approach leverages multiple expert modules and a gating mechanism to improve multi-task learning and enable uncertainty-aware trajectory estimation, addressing challenges like cumulative drift and poor robustness in inertial sensor-based localization. The framework exploits the mechanical link between the bike's pedals and rear wheel to relate the rider's pedaling patterns to acceleration changes, converting these into wheel speed for dynamic calibration. Testing with real-world data from DiDi's shared bikes showed a minimum 12% improvement in accuracy over baseline methods, with wheel speed errors kept below 0.5 m/s at the 95th percentile, demonstrating its potential for large-scale deployment in complex urban settings.

items.title: Researchers evaluate six defenses against persistent memory attacks on nine open-source stateful LLM agents, finding memory-layer tool-gating reduces attack success to zero in most cases [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers conducted a systematic evaluation of six defense mechanisms against persistent memory attacks on nine open-source stateful large language model (LLM) agents. These attacks involve malicious instructions injected through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) documents that persist in memory and execute in later sessions. The study found that most defenses, including input-level and retrieval-level filtering, failed to reduce attack success rates, which remained around 88-89%. However, a memory-layer defense called tool-gating (Memory Sandbox) effectively reduced attack success to zero in eight of the nine models by disabling the recall capability necessary for the attack.

items.title: Researchers propose FBOS-RL, a feedback-driven bi-objective reinforcement learning method that improves training efficiency and performance ceiling over GRPO by using feedback-guided exploration and dual objectives EPA and ECC [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced FBOS-RL, a feedback-driven bi-objective reinforcement learning method designed to enhance training efficiency and performance compared to the existing GRPO algorithm. FBOS-RL incorporates Feedback-Guided Exploration Enhancement and two synergistic training objectives, EPA and ECC, which together create a positive feedback loop that improves learning outcomes. This approach addresses the limitation of traditional RL methods that rely on sampling from the same prompt, which can hinder progress when tasks exceed the model's current capabilities. Extensive experiments show that FBOS-RL learns faster and achieves a higher performance ceiling than GRPO and other feedback-based baselines, maintaining higher policy entropy and lower gradient norms throughout training. By leveraging environment feedback to guide exploration and optimizing dual objectives, FBOS-RL offers a significant advancement in reinforcement learning for large-scale models.

items.title: Researchers introduce CARE, an auditable controller that improves LLM-generated policy selection in scientific experimentation, boosting benchmark performance on Minerva/Olympus and ChemLex datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed CARE, an auditable controller designed to improve policy selection generated by large language models (LLMs) in scientific experimentation. CARE maintains a non-LLM incumbent optimizer as the default while allowing LLMs to propose challenger policies, which are only authorized if supported by pre-selection evidence recorded in an audit log. This approach enhances safety and stability in costly, irreversible experiments by preventing unsafe exploration. CARE demonstrated superior performance on the Minerva/Olympus and ChemLex benchmarks, increasing final-best scores from 80.0 to 88.5 and 83.9 to 92.1 respectively, compared to the incumbent optimizer. The study suggests that LLMs are more effective when expanding the proposal space under an auditable controller rather than directly selecting experiments, enabling more reliable self-evolution in high-throughput experimentation optimization.

items.title: Researchers propose Skill-MAS, an evolvable Meta-Skill framework for automatic multi-agent systems that improves performance and experience retention across multiple LLMs and benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Skill-MAS, a new framework designed to enhance automatic Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) that use Large Language Models (LLMs). Skill-MAS addresses the challenge of balancing model capability with experience retention by treating high-level orchestration as an evolvable Meta-Skill, which is refined through a closed optimization loop involving behavioral sampling and selective reflection. This approach improves performance and experience retention without relying on traditional parametric updates. The framework was tested across four complex benchmarks and with four different LLMs, demonstrating significant performance improvements and efficient cost-performance trade-offs. Additionally, the evolved Meta-Skills showed robustness and strong transferability to new tasks and different LLMs, suggesting broad applicability and scalability for complex multi-agent tasks.

items.title: Researchers present NeuroShield, a device-agnostic foundation model for EEG authentication pretrained on 15,762 subjects across three datasets, improving error rates and generalizing across hardware and recording variations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed NeuroShield, a device-agnostic foundation model for EEG authentication that addresses the challenge of variability in headset hardware, channel layouts, and signal durations. Pretrained on data from 15,762 subjects across three public EEG datasets, NeuroShield uses a dual-stage transformer architecture to learn identity-discriminative embeddings from recordings with varying channels and lengths. After fine-tuning, it significantly reduces error rates compared to existing methods and generalizes well to new datasets and recording conditions. NeuroShield's design overcomes the fragmentation in EEG authentication models that typically require separate development for each new device or dataset. It operates effectively across different channel configurations and longer signal segments than those seen during training, demonstrating strong adaptability. The model is released as open source to encourage reproducibility and wider adoption within the research community.

items.title: Researchers propose Ramanujan Propagation, a graph rewiring method using Ramanujan graphs with non-negative resistance curvature to reduce over-squashing in Graph Neural Networks and improve message passing efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Ramanujan Propagation, a novel graph rewiring method that uses Ramanujan graphs with non-negative resistance curvature to address the over-squashing problem in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). This approach improves the efficiency of message passing by reducing topological bottlenecks, enabling better learning of long-range dependencies in graph-structured data. The team developed an algorithmic framework to construct Ramanujan-rewired graphs that maintain the original graph's local connectivity while enhancing information flow. Experimental results show that this method outperforms nine existing state-of-the-art rewiring techniques, establishing Ramanujan graphs as a robust structural prior for scalable and topology-aware message passing in GNNs.

items.title: Researchers find knowledge editing in large language models often fails to fully erase facts, acting as suppression rather than removal, and is vulnerable to adversarial attacks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have found that knowledge editing (KE) techniques used to update specific facts in large language models (LLMs) often fail to completely erase the original information. Instead of removing facts, these methods tend to suppress them, allowing the original knowledge to resurface. This issue persists across various model architectures and raises concerns about the reliability of KE approaches. The study reveals that popular KE methods, which rely on low-rank updates, do not overwrite existing knowledge but redistribute it within the model's representation space. Edited knowledge resides in narrow, sensitive regions of the model's loss landscape, making it vulnerable to indirect prompting and adversarial attacks. These findings highlight fundamental architectural weaknesses in current KE algorithms and suggest a need to reconsider how post-hoc updates are applied in LLM applications.

items.title: The Economist examines whether artificial intelligence authored its June 2026 article amid debates on AI content creation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The Economist published an article in June 2026 that questions whether artificial intelligence was responsible for writing its content, highlighting ongoing debates about AI's involvement in content creation and authorship. The piece reflects broader discussions on the evolving role of AI in journalism and the challenges of attributing authorship in the digital age.

items.title: Researchers propose G-SPIN, a graph neural network and large language model framework for phonetic error correction in noisy automatic speech recognition systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced G-SPIN, a novel framework that enhances phonetic error correction in automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems by combining graph neural networks with large language models. This approach targets residual lexical errors, particularly those affecting critical tokens like named entities and sentiment words, which often arise from phonetic similarities rather than random noise. G-SPIN constructs phonetic candidate neighborhoods using a graph neural network, applies a masked language model for local context scoring, and uses an instruction-tuned large language model for final context-aware re-ranking, improving correction accuracy while avoiding unconstrained generation. The framework operates entirely at inference time and is designed to be lightweight and modular. By separating phonetic reasoning from semantic context selection, G-SPIN effectively narrows the correction search space to acoustically plausible alternatives, addressing structured errors that traditional token-level correction methods struggle to fix.

items.title: Researchers introduce AgentOdyssey, a framework generating open-ended long-horizon text games to evaluate test-time continual learning agents' exploration, memory, and planning abilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed AgentOdyssey, a new evaluation framework designed to test the abilities of continual learning agents in open-ended, long-horizon text games. This framework challenges agents to explore, acquire knowledge, retain episodic memories, and plan effectively while learning continuously during deployment, moving beyond traditional assumptions that learning does not occur at test time. AgentOdyssey generates complex text-based environments with rich dynamics and tasks, providing a multifaceted evaluation that measures game progress alongside diagnostic tests of key agent capabilities such as memory, exploration, and action diversity. The study assessed various agent paradigms using AgentOdyssey, revealing significant limitations in their exploration, memory retention, and planning skills. Although stronger base models improved performance, even the best agents fell short of human-level proficiency, indicating substantial room for advancement. The findings also highlight the importance of short-term memory in enhancing agent performance during test-time training, suggesting it as a critical component for future continual learning systems.

items.title: Survey analyzes LLM-based scientific peer review methods, benchmarks, and reliability challenges including robustness risks and evaluation limitations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent survey examines the use of large language models (LLMs) in scientific peer review, addressing their potential to assist with critique generation and score prediction amid the increasing volume of submissions. The study categorizes various modeling approaches and reviews empirical results from existing benchmarks, highlighting limitations in datasets, evaluation methods, and domain biases that affect current assessments. The survey also identifies significant risks to the robustness and security of automated review systems, such as prompt injection, data poisoning, and reward hacking, which could lead to manipulation. It discusses challenges in handling subjective disagreements and cross-domain generalization, proposing a framework to develop more reliable, transparent, and trustworthy AI-assisted peer review processes.

items.title: Researchers propose SALSA method for single-pass machine-generated code detection, achieving 0.789 out-of-distribution F1 score at SemEval-2026 Task 13, outperforming CodeBERT baseline [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced a new method called SALSA (Single-pass Autoregressive LLM Structured Classification) for detecting machine-generated code in the SemEval-2026 Task 13 Subtask A. This approach treats the detection as a binary classification problem over code snippets, focusing on generalizing to unseen programming languages and application domains. SALSA trains the model to produce a single-token label for each class, delegating the authorship decision to the model itself rather than relying on handcrafted features or rules. To enhance robustness against out-of-distribution data, the team employed balanced sampling across languages, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and conservative training strategies to prevent overfitting. Their best system achieved an out-of-distribution F1 score of 0.789 on the official leaderboard, significantly outperforming the CodeBERT baseline, which scored 0.305.

items.title: Researchers develop a codebook to analyze cognitive, affective, and behavioral self-stigma in 72,115 Reddit posts by people who use drugs, finding behavioral indicators often precede internalized stigma [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers developed a detailed codebook to analyze self-stigma expressed in cognitive, affective, and behavioral terms among people who use drugs, examining 72,115 Reddit posts from 1,660 users. They identified ten key indicators of self-stigma, such as self-labeling and despair, and found that behavioral signs often appear before internalized feelings like shame. The study revealed that self-stigma is an integrated phenomenon where behavioral expressions rarely occur without internalized stigma, and most indicators remain stable over time except for increasing pessimism about change. The team used a combination of expert coding and a large language model to classify posts, achieving substantial agreement and accuracy. Their analysis showed that 5.3% of posts contained self-stigma, with 74% of users expressing it at least once. Contrary to traditional progressive models of stigma development, behavioral indicators like the desire to quit emerged earlier than core emotional indicators. This finding suggests that early behavioral signs could serve as targets for digital interventions aimed at reducing self-stigma among people who use drugs online.

items.title: Researchers present a method using parsing expression grammars to structure the Arabic-English Al-Mawrid dictionary into machine-readable hierarchical entries [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a method to convert the Arabic-English Al-Mawrid dictionary into a machine-readable format by structuring its entries into hierarchical components. Using parsing expression grammars, the method transforms dictionary entries from plain text into organized structures that explicitly represent subentries, defining phrases, domain labels, cross-references, and translation equivalents. This approach addresses the challenge that printed dictionaries are designed for human use rather than machine processing. The method involves cascaded steps with parsing as the central process, implemented through a parser based on parsing expression grammars formalism. Despite the lack of standardized microstructure in Arabic dictionaries, the study demonstrates that it is feasible to automatically or semi-automatically structure such dictionaries with reasonable accuracy after analyzing their microstructure.

items.title: Researchers apply prompt-based learning with ChatGPT and other models to automatically generate academic paper highlights, achieving results comparable to supervised methods without large labeled datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a prompt-based learning approach using ChatGPT and other language models to automatically generate highlights for academic papers, achieving results comparable to traditional supervised methods without requiring large labeled datasets. This method uses task-specific prompt templates combined with paper abstracts as inputs and has been tested on multiple datasets, showing strong performance especially when a few examples are included in the prompts. The study evaluates models like GPT-2, T5, and ChatGPT accessed via API, finding that ChatGPT's performance is highly sensitive to prompt design despite its strong language capabilities. Generated highlights are generally coherent and informative, closely matching author-written summaries. This approach does not depend on domain-specific training data, enabling highlight generation for papers lacking such information and supporting applications in literature retrieval, text mining, and bibliometric analysis.

items.title: Researchers present Hybrid-IR, a dual-path retrieval framework with iterative reasoning combining graph-based and dense retrieval for complex medical question answering, demonstrating effectiveness on three benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Hybrid-IR, a dual-path retrieval framework designed to improve complex medical question answering by combining graph-based and dense retrieval methods with an iterative reasoning process. This approach addresses limitations in current retrieval-augmented generation techniques, which often rely on a single retrieval path and static strategies that struggle with fragmented medical knowledge and deep reasoning requirements. Hybrid-IR integrates structured knowledge exploration and fine-grained semantic matching, refining its reasoning through iterative retrieval and reasoning loops. The effectiveness of Hybrid-IR was demonstrated through experiments on three widely used medical QA benchmarks, showing improved performance in handling complex queries. This framework offers a promising advancement in leveraging large language models for biomedical applications by mitigating issues related to hallucinations and outdated information through enhanced retrieval mechanisms.

items.title: Researchers introduce Local Branch Routing, a trainable token-level test-time scaling method for language models that improves reasoning efficiency and accuracy on mathematical benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Local Branch Routing (LBR), a novel token-level test-time scaling method for language models that enhances reasoning efficiency and accuracy, particularly on mathematical benchmarks. LBR constructs a small local lookahead tree and uses a lightweight router to select the most promising subtree, allowing each token decision to incorporate evidence beyond the immediate next-token prediction without requiring full solution-level search. This approach enables end-to-end reinforcement learning by defining a tractable tree-trajectory likelihood and jointly optimizing the base model and router. LBR's prune-shift-grow decoding process preserves discrete branch identities and assigns explicit probabilities to router decisions, facilitating verifiable rewards during training. Experiments on synthetic hierarchical-planning tasks demonstrate that hidden states after candidate generation provide valuable routing information. On mathematical reasoning tests, LBR outperforms existing methods such as discrete chain-of-thought and other reinforcement learning baselines, indicating that lightweight local branching offers an efficient, trainable, and discrete form of test-time scaling for language models.

items.title: Researchers present computational stylometry analysis of English Pali Canon across Sutta, Vinaya, and Abhidhamma Pitakas, revealing vocabulary diversity, Zipf distributions, and translation differences
items.content_text: Researchers conducted a computational stylometric analysis of the English translations of the Pali Canon, covering all three Pitakas: Sutta, Vinaya, and Abhidhamma.
