The study analyzed over 134,000 text segments from multiple translations and traditions, examining vocabulary diversity, Zipf rank-frequency distributions, numeral-word density, and vocabulary overlap. Key findings include consistent Zipf distributions across corpora, similar lexical diversity between Sutta and Vinaya Theravada texts, higher diversity and numeral density in the Abhidhamma corpus, and notable vocabulary differences between translations and traditions.

items.title: Research decomposes geometric transformations from original novels to sequels using sentence embeddings across 13 author pairs, revealing taxonomy of sequel types and structural narrative shifts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers analyzed the geometric transformations between original novels and their sequels by representing books as points in a sentence-embedding space. Using paragraph embeddings from the PG19 corpus and principal component analysis, they decomposed the differences between original and sequel texts across thirteen author pairs, identifying distinct sequel types such as formulaic, concentrated, and compositional transformations. This approach revealed structural narrative shifts, exemplified by the transition from "Tom Sawyer" to "Huckleberry Finn," where the dominant change reflected a move from domestic settings to a picaresque journey rather than surface themes. The study corroborated these geometric findings with historical authorial intent, notably Mark Twain's letters outlining his narrative goals, and quantified how much of the sequel's transformation aligned with these intentions. All analyses are reproducible with the provided scripts and data, offering a novel framework for understanding literary sequel development through computational methods.

items.title: Survey analyzes toxicity detection and mitigation methods for multilingual large language models, highlighting challenges in language coverage, cultural harm definitions, and evaluation consistency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent survey examines toxicity detection and mitigation strategies for multilingual large language models (LLMs), highlighting challenges in ensuring consistent safety across diverse linguistic and cultural contexts. The study reviews threat models that exploit language features and deployment scenarios to bypass safety measures, and categorizes approaches for toxicity detection and detoxification, including various task formulations and mitigation techniques. The survey identifies key issues such as uneven language coverage, culturally specific definitions of harm, inconsistent evaluation protocols, and the potential for detoxification methods to inadvertently suppress legitimate dialects or identity-related expressions. These findings underscore the complexity of developing effective and culturally sensitive safety mechanisms for multilingual LLMs.

items.title: Researchers release Hlava Cor and Hlava AD corpora with multiple Czech text annotations showing 60-65% inter-annotator agreement on coreference and discourse relations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed two new Czech language corpora, Hlava Cor and Hlava AD, to study variations in human annotation of coreference and discourse relations. The Hlava Cor corpus includes 1,024 contexts annotated by three annotators focusing on coreference across different text types and grammatical categories, while the Hlava AD corpus contains 512 contexts annotated by five annotators targeting discourse relations in various constructions. Both corpora show an inter-annotator agreement of about 60-65%, highlighting the variability in human interpretation of text coherence. The study found that agreement on coreference annotations tends to be lower in cases where automatic coreference resolution models also disagree, indicating these examples are more challenging or ambiguous for both humans and machines. Annotators provided explanations for their choices, revealing differences in interpretation, confidence levels, and reading strategies, which underscores the complexity of understanding discourse phenomena in natural language processing.

items.title: Researchers propose Agent-Authored World Modeling to align LLM agent training with decision-relevant dynamics instead of next-observation prediction, validated across multiple environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced Agent-Authored World Modeling (AAWM), a new training approach for Large Language Model (LLM) agents that focuses on aligning the learning objective with the agent's decision-making needs rather than predicting the next observation. AAWM enables the agent to identify relevant environmental dynamics necessary for its current decisions and uses this information to guide training targets, improving the relevance of the learned world model. The method involves retrieving and synthesizing transition evidence based on the agent's policy requirements at each state, shifting supervision from next-observation reconstruction to capturing decision-oriented dynamics. Experimental validation across various environments and training settings demonstrates that AAWM provides a more effective learning signal than traditional next-observation prediction, enhancing the agent's ability to model the world in a way that supports sequential decision making.

items.title: Researchers propose PolicyAlign, a framework for direct policy-based safety alignment of large language models using synthesized violations and self-distillation, improving safety across multiple domains [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced PolicyAlign, a new framework designed to directly align large language models (LLMs) with evolving safety policies expressed in natural language. Unlike traditional methods that rely on high-quality supervision data, PolicyAlign synthesizes policy-violating instructions and uses on-policy self-distillation to internalize policy-guided behavior, addressing the challenge of costly or unavailable supervision data in real-world deployments. The framework incorporates Policy-Sensitive Filtering to enhance training stability and data efficiency by focusing on instructions that cause the largest behavioral changes. Experiments demonstrate that PolicyAlign improves safety across multiple models while maintaining general capabilities and minimizing unnecessary refusals. It also generalizes effectively to specialized domains such as medical, legal, and financial contexts, suggesting its potential as a scalable and maintainable approach for policy-based safety alignment in LLMs. The researchers have made the code publicly available for further development and application.

items.title: Researchers analyze self-supervised speech model's articulatory feature representations across Mandarin sub-dialects using unsupervised, language-agnostic probing revealing dialect-dependent variation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers conducted a study on a self-supervised speech model to analyze how its internal phonetic representations vary across Mandarin sub-dialects. Using an unsupervised, language-agnostic probing method that employs a universal phone recognizer and articulatory feature mapping, they examined articulatory feature decodability without relying on manual annotations. The study found that while some features like labiality and stridency remain stable, others related to finer spectral distinctions show significant dialect-dependent variation, particularly with higher decodability in Beijing speech compared to other sub-dialects. The analysis also revealed distinct representational dynamics across different layers of the model for various articulatory features. These findings demonstrate that language-agnostic articulatory probing can effectively be applied to natural dialect speech corpora and highlight that sensitivity to dialectal differences in self-supervised speech representations is unevenly distributed across articulatory dimensions.

items.title: Researchers fine-tune PEGASUS on XL-Sum English corpus, achieving up to 15.25% ROUGE-2 score improvement over baseline mT5 model in abstractive summarization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have fine-tuned the PEGASUS transformer model on the XL-Sum English corpus for abstractive text summarization, achieving significant improvements over the baseline mT5 model. The fine-tuned PEGASUS model demonstrated a 15.25% increase in the ROUGE-2 score, along with improvements in ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-L scores, indicating more accurate and concise summary generation compared to previous approaches. Abstractive summarization involves generating brief summaries that capture the key ideas of a source text without simply extracting sentences. The study evaluated the model's performance using the ROUGE metric, which compares machine-generated summaries to human-created ones. These results represent a state-of-the-art performance on the XL-Sum English corpus, highlighting the effectiveness of fine-tuning PEGASUS for this task.

items.title: Study finds 18.6% of Sri Lankan tourism reviews show mismatch between star ratings and textual sentiment, with venue type and reviewer behavior as key factors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A study analyzing 16,156 Sri Lankan tourism attraction reviews from 2010 to 2023 found that 18.6% of reviews show a mismatch between star ratings and the sentiment expressed in the review text. Using a transformer-based sentiment analysis, the research identified six patterns of incongruence, with behaviors like Conservative Rater and Obligatory 5-Star contributing most to the discrepancies. The mismatch rates also varied by venue type, with museums exhibiting the highest levels of rating-text divergence. The study employed statistical tests, logistic regression, Random Forest, and SHAP analysis to determine that factors such as venue type, reviewer expertise, review length, and timing influence the inconsistency between ratings and textual sentiment. The findings highlight that star ratings should not be assumed to directly reflect textual sentiment and must be validated before being used as ground-truth labels in natural language processing applications.

items.title: Researchers develop Riazi-8B, an Urdu large language model for mathematical reasoning, using Urdu Wikipedia pre-training and Chain-of-Thought fine-tuning to improve performance on MGSM-Urdu benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed Riazi-8B, a large language model designed to enhance mathematical reasoning in Urdu, a low-resource language. The model was created through a two-step process involving continued pre-training on Urdu Wikipedia and supervised fine-tuning using Urdu Chain-of-Thought data derived from GSM8K. Evaluations on the MGSM-Urdu benchmark show that Riazi-8B outperforms existing Urdu instruction-tuned models in answer accuracy, reasoning quality, response completeness, and Urdu language generation. This development addresses the scarcity of reasoning-oriented datasets and models for Urdu, which has limited the application of recent advances in mathematical reasoning to Urdu-speaking users. The study demonstrates that combining language-specific adaptation with reasoning-focused fine-tuning effectively extends mathematical reasoning capabilities to languages with limited resources.

items.title: Researchers report tool calling suppression in open-weight LLMs under simultaneous JSON Schema constraints, propose two-pass execution to restore tool use without retraining [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called Tool Suppression in open-weight large language models (LLMs) when tool calling and JSON Schema constraints are applied simultaneously. This issue causes models to stop invoking tools despite maintaining high compliance with schema constraints. The study, conducted across multiple model families and deployment settings, reveals that JSON Schema constraints create token masks that block tool-call tokens during decoding, explaining the suppression behavior. To address this, the researchers propose the Constraint Priority Inversion hypothesis, suggesting that schema satisfaction may override action selection under multiple constraints. They introduce a Transparent Two-Pass Execution method that separates tool execution from schema-constrained response generation, restoring tool use without retraining the models. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating tool use and structured output jointly to ensure reliability in production agent systems. The associated code and data will be made publicly available.

items.title: Researchers propose MedGuards, a multi-agent system for medical error detection and correction using confidence-guided arbitration, improving accuracy across multilingual clinical datasets without retraining base LLMs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed MedGuards, a multi-agent system designed to improve the detection and correction of medical errors in text generated by large language models (LLMs). This framework uses specialized agents to identify, locate, and correct errors, with a confidence-guided arbitration mechanism to resolve conflicts, enhancing accuracy without retraining the base models. MedGuards was tested on four multilingual clinical datasets, showing significant improvements in error correction performance. The system introduces a new evaluation metric called the Keyword-Prioritized Correction Score (KPCS), which focuses on the accurate generation of critical keywords in medical texts, offering a more comprehensive assessment than traditional metrics. By improving interpretability, robustness, and adaptability, MedGuards aims to support safer deployment of LLMs in healthcare settings. The researchers have made their code publicly available to facilitate reproducibility and further development.

items.title: Researchers present BITEMBED, a low-bit LLM text embedding framework using ternary weights and quantized activations to reduce storage and inference costs while maintaining performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced BITEMBED, a low-bit framework designed to improve the efficiency of large language model (LLM) text embedders by reducing storage and inference costs while maintaining performance. BITEMBED transforms pretrained LLM backbones into embedding encoders with ternary weights and quantized activations, optimizing both encoding speed and vector storage. The model undergoes continual contrastive pre-training and supervised fine-tuning using distillation techniques from a full-precision teacher model. BITEMBED also supports multiple storage precisions for output embeddings, allowing flexibility to meet different storage requirements. Experiments using Qwen3-0.6B and Gemma3-270M models on the MMTEB benchmark demonstrate that BITEMBED achieves performance comparable to full-precision embedders, offering a practical trade-off between embedding quality and resource consumption.
